Accordingly, in that remarkable vision which Isaiah describes, (Isaiah 6:3,) the cherubim cry out — “Holy, holy, holy, Lord God of Hosts.” And in several other places of Scripture the angels are represented as praising God by such ascription’s. How, then, can zeal like theirs stand in need of exhortations? Or, if they require to be incited, what can be more unseemly than that we, who are so sluggish in the service, should assume the part of exhorting them to their duty? David, then, who did not equal the angels in zeal, but came far behind them, was not qualified to be an exhorter to them. But neither did this enter into his purpose; he would simply testify that it was the height of his happiness and desire to join in sacred concert with elect angels in praising God. And there is nothing unreasonable that, in order to stir himself up in the praises of God, he should call as companions upon the angels, although these run spontaneously in the service, and are fitter to lead the way. He calls them, in the second part of the verse — <span style="color:#800000">*the armies of God;*</span> for they stand always ready to receive his orders. “Ten thousand times ten thousand surround his throne,” as Daniel says, (Daniel 7:10.) The same name is applied also to the stars, both because they are remarkable for the order which maintains among them, and because they execute with inconceivable quickness the orders of God. But the angels are here called armies, upon the same account as elsewhere principalities and powers, inasmuch as God exerts his power by their hands.

**3.** <span style="color:#800000">*Praise him, ye sun and moon*</span>. This passage gives no countenance to the dream of Plato, that the stars excel in sense and intelligence. Nor does the Psalmist give them the same place as he had just assigned to angels, but merely intimates that the glory of God is everywhere to be seen, as if they sang his praises with an audible voice. And here he tacitly reproves the ingratitude of man; for all would hear this symphony, were they at all attent upon considering the works of God. For doth not the sun by his light, and heat, and other marvelous effects, praise his Maker? The stars when they run their course, and at once adorn the heavens and give light to the earth, do they not sound the praises of God? but as we are deaf and insensible, the Psalmist calls upon them as witnesses to reprove our indolence. By the <span style="color:#800000">*heavens of heavens*</span> he no doubt means the spheres. Eclipses, and other things which we observe, plainly show both that the fixed stars are above the planets, and that the planets themselves are placed in different orbits. <span style="color:#800000">FE297A</span> The excellency of this contrivance the Psalmist justly commends, speaking expressly of the heavens of heavens;

<!-- PAGE 834 -->

not as if there were really more heavens than one, but to extol the matchless wisdom which God has shown in creating the heavens; for the sun, moon, and stars are not confusedly mixed together, but each has its own position and station assigned to it, and their manifold courses are all regulated. As under the name of <span style="color:#800000">*the heavens*</span> he comprehends the air, or at least all the space from the middle region of the air upwards, he calls rains, <span style="color:#800000">*the waters above the heavens*</span>. There is no foundation for the conjecture which some have made, that there are waters deposited above the four elements; and when the Psalmist speaks of these waters as being above, he clearly points at the descent of the rain. It is adhering too strictly to the letter of the words employed, to conceive as if there were some sea up in the heavens, where the waters were permanently deposited; for we know that Moses and the Prophets ordinarily speak in a popular style, suited to the lowest apprehension. It would be absurd, then, to seek to reduce what they say to the rules of philosophy; as, for example, in the passage before us, the Psalmist notes the marvelous fact that God holds the waters suspended in the air, because it seems contrary to nature that they should mount aloft, and also, that though fluid they should hang in vacant space. Accordingly it is said elsewhere, that they are held there as enclosed in bottles. (Psalm 33:7.) The Psalmist has borrowed the form of expression from Moses, who says — “that the waters were divided from the waters.” (Genesis 1:6.)

<!-- PAGE 835 -->
**5.** <span style="color:#800000">*Let them praise the name*</span>, etc. As he speaks of things wanting intelligence, he passes to the third person, from which we infer that his reason for having spoken in the second person hitherto, was to make a deeper impression upon men. And he asks no other praise than that which may teach us that the stars did not make themselves, nor the rains spring from chance; for notwithstanding the signal proofs we constantly have before our eyes of the divine power, we with shameful carelessness overlook the great author. He says emphatically — <span style="color:#800000">*for He Himself created,*</span> intimating that the world is not eternal, as wicked men conjecture, nor made by a concourse of atoms, but that this fair order of things which we see, suddenly sprang forth upon the commandment of God. And, speaking of the creation, he adds what is even more worthy of observation, that he gave that law to them which remains inviolable. For many, while they grant that the world was made by God, lapse from this into the senseless notion that now the order of nature stands of itself, and that God sits idle in the heavens. The Psalmist very properly insists, therefore, that the works of God above us in the heavens were not only made by him, but even now move forward at his disposal; and that not only was a secret power communicated to them at first, but while they go through their assigned parts, their operation and ministry to their various ends is dependent upon God.

## <19E807>PSALM 148:7-10

**7.** Praise Jehovah! ye creatures from the earth, <span style="color:#800000">FE298A</span> dragons, <span style="color:#800000">FE299A</span> and all deeps. 8. Fire and hail, snow and ice, breath of the storm doing his word. 9. Mountains, and all hills; fruitful tree, and all cedars. 10. Wild beasts, and all cattle; reptile, and winged fowl.

<!-- PAGE 836 -->
**7.** <span style="color:#800000">*Praise Jehovah*</span>, etc. He now comes to the lower parts of the world; although deviating at the same time from the exact order, he mixes up such things as are produced in the air — lightning’s, snow, ice, and storms. These should rather have been placed among the former class, but he has respect to the common apprehension of men. The scope of the whole is, that wherever we turn our eyes we meet with evidences of the power of God. He speaks first of <span style="color:#800000">*the whales*</span>; for, as he mentions the *abysses* or <span style="color:#800000">*deeps*</span> immediately afterwards, I have no doubt that by <span style="color:#008080">תנינים</span>, *tanninim*, he means fishes of the sea, such as whales. It is only reasonable to think that matter for praising God should be taken from the sea, which is fraught with so many wonders. He then ascends to <span style="color:#800000">*hail, snows*</span>, and <span style="color:#800000">*storms*</span>, which he says <span style="color:#800000">*fulfill the word of God*</span>; for it is not by an effect of chance that the heavens are clouded, or that a single drop of rain falls from the clouds, or that the thunders rage, but one and all of these changes depend upon the secret will of God, whether he will show his goodness to the children of men in irrigating the earth, or punish their sins by tempest, hail, or other calamities. The passage contains instruction of various kinds, as, for example, that when dearth impends, however parched the earth may be by long continued heat, God can promptly send rain which will remove the drought at his pleasure. If from incessant rains, on the other hand, the seed rot in the ground, or the crops do not come to maturity, we should pray for fair weather. If we are alarmed by thunder, we are taught to pray to God, for as it is he who sends it in his anger, so he can still all the troubled elements. And we are not to take up the narrow view of this truth which irreligious men advocate, that things in nature merely move according to the laws impressed upon them from the beginning, while God stands by idle, but are to hold firmly that God watches over his creatures, and that nothing can take place without his present disposal, as we have seen, <span style="color:#800000"><19A404></span>Psalm 104:4 that

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#000080">“he maketh the winds his messengers,</span> <span style="color:#000080">and his ministers a flaming fire.”</span></p>

## <19E811>PSALM 148:11-14

**11.** Kings of the earth, and all peoples; princes, and all judges of the earth. 12. Young men, and also virgins; old men, with children. 13. Let them praise the name of Jehovah: for exalted is his name only, his praise is above the earth and the heavens. 14. And he hath exalted the horn of his people: praise is to all his merciful ones, to the children of Israel, a people which is near to him. Hallelujah.

<!-- PAGE 837 -->
**11.** <span style="color:#800000">*Kings of the earth*</span>, etc. He now turns his address to men, with a respect to whom it was that he called for a declaration of God’s praises from creatures, both above and from beneath. As kings and princes are blinded by the dazzling influence of their station, so as to think the world was made for them, and to despise God in the pride of their hearts, he particularly calls them to this duty; and, by mentioning them first, he reproves their ingratitude in withholding their tribute of praise when they are under greater obligations than others. As all men originally stand upon a level as to condition, the higher persons have risen, and the nearer they have been brought to God, the more sacredly are they bound to proclaim his goodness. The more intolerable is the wickedness of kings and princes who claim exemption from the common rule, when they ought rather to inculcate it upon others and lead the way. He could have addressed his exhortation at once summarily to all men, as indeed he mentions *peoples* in general terms; but by thrice specifying <span style="color:#800000">*princes*</span> he suggests that they are slow to discharge the duty, and need to be urged do it. Then follows a division according to age and sex, to show that all without exception are created for this end, and should unitedly devote their energies to it. As to <span style="color:#800000">*old men*</span>, the more God has lengthened out their lives the more should they be exercised in singing his praises; but he joins <span style="color:#800000">*young men*</span> with them, for though they have less experience from continued habit, it will be inexcusable if they do not acknowledge the great mercy of God in the vigor of their lives. In speaking of *girls* or <span style="color:#800000">*virgins*</span>, the particle <span style="color:#008080">גם</span>, *gam, also*, is not merely expletive, but added to make the words more emphatical, conveying the truth that even the young women who are not so liberally educated as the male sex, being considered as born for domestic offices, will omit their duty if they do not join with the rest of the Church in praising God. It follows that all from the least to the greatest are bound by this common rule.

**14.** <span style="color:#800000">*And hath exalted the horn*</span>, etc. As we saw in the former Psalm, that the perfections of God are to be seen more conspicuously in the Church than in the constitution of the world at large, the Psalmist has added this sentence, as to the Church being protected by the divine hand, and armed with a power against all enemies which secures its safety in every danger. By <span style="color:#800000">*the horn*</span>, as is well known, is meant strength or dignity. Accordingly the Psalmist means that God’s blessing is apparent in his Church and among his chosen people, inasmuch as it only flourishes and is powerful through his strength. There is a tacit comparison implied between the Church of God and other hostile powers, for it needs divine guardianship as being exposed on all sides to attack. Hence the Psalmist infers that <span style="color:#800000">*praise is to all the merciful ones of God*</span>, for they have ground given them in the singular goodness of his condescension both for self-congratulation and praise. In calling the children of Israel a <span style="color:#800000">*people near unto God,*</span> he reminds them of the gracious covenant which God made with Abraham. For how came the nearness, except in the way of God’s preferring an unknown despised stranger to all nations? Nor are we to seek the cause of the distinction elsewhere than in the mere love of God. Though all the world equally belongs to God, he graciously discovered himself to the children of Israel, and brought them near to him, strangers as they were from God, even as are the whole race of Adam. Hence the words of Moses —

<!-- PAGE 838 -->

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#000080">“When the Most High divided to the nations their inheritance, and</span> <span style="color:#000080">distributed the peoples, he stretched forth his line to Jacob.”</span> <span style="color:#000080">(</span><span style="color:#000080">Deuteronomy 32:8.)</span></p>

He is to be considered, therefore, as pointing out the cause why God hath extended such signal blessings to a single people, and a people poor and despised — his adoption of them to himself.

<!-- PAGE 839 -->

<p class="title-block-h1" style="text-align:center; font-size:22px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#0000d4">PSALM 149</span></p>

If we may be allowed to compare this Psalm with the former ones, and the next, which is the last, the only difference is, that while the author of the Psalm, whoever he was, has hitherto spoken of God’s special care and protection of his Church in connection with the common providential government of the world, here he speaks of his benefits to the Church exclusively. In the next Psalm mention is only made of the power of God in general.

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*Hallelujah.*</span></p>

## <19E901>PSALM 149:1-4

**1.** Sing ye to Jehovah a new song: his praise is in the congregation of the merciful. 2. Let Israel rejoice in his Maker: let the sons of Zion rejoice their king. <span style="color:#800000">fe291</span> 3. Let them praise his name on the pipe, <span style="color:#800000">fe292</span> on the timbrel <span style="color:#800000">fe293</span> and the harp let them sing psalms to him. 4. Because Jehovah hath taken pleasure in his people; he will glorify the poor unto salvation.

<!-- PAGE 840 -->
**1.** <span style="color:#800000">*Sing to Jehovah a new song.*</span> This exordium proves what I have just said, that the exhortation now given is addressed only to God’s people; for the singular goodness which is particularly extended to them affords more ample matter of praise. The probable conjecture is, that the Psalm was composed at the time when the people were begun to rejoice, or after they had returned to their native country from the Babylonish captivity. We will see from the context that a promise is given of recovery from their ruined condition. The object, I think, of the Psalmist, is to encourage them to expect the full and complete deliverance, some prelude of which had been suddenly and unexpectedly given in the permission to return. As the Church was not fully restored at once, but was with difficulty and only after a long period brought to a state of vigor, comfort such as this was much needed. The Spirit of God would also furnish a remedy for evils which were afterwards to break out; for the Church had scarcely begun to respire when it was again harassed with various evils, and oppressed by the cruel tyranny of Antiochus, which was followed up by a dreadful dispersion. The Psalmist had good reason therefore for animating the godly to look forward for the full accomplishment of the mercy of God, that they might be persuaded of divine protection until such time as the Messiah should arise who would gather all Israel. He calls this <span style="color:#800000">*a new song*</span>, as we have noticed elsewhere, to distinguish it from those with which the saints commonly and daily praised God, for praise is their continued exercise. It follows that he speaks of some rare and unusual benefit, demanding signal and particular thanksgiving. And I am disposed to think that whoever may have been the author of the Psalm, he alludes to that passage in Isaiah, (Isaiah 42:10,) “Sing unto the Lord a new song,” when he speaks of the future restoration of the Church, and the eternal kingdom of Christ. In the second clause of the verse there is a promise implied. For though he proceeds to exhort the Lord’s people to sing God’s praises together, he hints along with this that the Church would coalesce again into one body, so as to celebrate God’s praises in the solemn assembly. We know that so scattered were the Israelites, that the sacred songs ceased to be sung, as elsewhere they complain of being called upon to sing —

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#000080">“How shall we sing the songs of the Lord in a strange land?”</span> <span style="color:#000080">(</span><span style="color:#800000"><19D704></span><span style="color:#000080">Psalm 137:4.)</span></p>

He bids them prepare therefore after this sad dispersion for holding their sacred assemblies again.

<!-- PAGE 841 -->
**2.** <span style="color:#800000">*Let Israel rejoice in his Maker.*</span> He insists upon the same point, that the Lord’s people should rest firmly persuaded that their family had not been chosen out in vain from the rest of the world, but that God would be mindful of his covenant, and not allow the mercies which he had extended to them to fail or become extinct. Although they had been temporarily deprived of the inheritance of the land of Canaan, which was the pledge of their adoption, the Psalmist calls God their <span style="color:#800000">*Maker, and king of the sons of Zion,*</span> to remind them that when adopted to a pre-eminency above other nations, this was a species of new creation. So in Psalm 45:6, the Israelites are called “the work of God’s hands,” not merely because they were like other men created by him, but because he had formed them anew, and distinguished them with a new honor, that, of being separated front the whole human race. The name king has a wider signification, intimating that as this people was at first formed by God, so it was with the view of their being ever governed by his power. The musical instruments he mentions were peculiar to this infancy of the Church, nor should we foolishly imitate a practice which was intended only for God’s ancient people. But the Psalmist confirms what has been already mentioned, that their religious assemblies which had been for a time interrupted would soon be restored, and they would call upon the name of the Lord in the due order of his worship.

**4.** <span style="color:#800000">*For God hath taken pleasure in his people.*</span> We have spoken elsewhere of the verb <span style="color:#008080">רצה</span>, *ratsah* here it means *free favor,* the Psalmist saying that it was entirely of his good pleasure that God had chosen this people to himself. From this source flows what is added in the second clause, that God would give a new glory of deliverance to the afflicted. In the Hebrew <span style="color:#008080">ענוים</span>, *anavim,* means *poor and afflicted ones,* but the term came afterwards to be applied to *merciful persons,* as bodily afflictions have a tendency to subdue pride, while abundance begets cruelty. The Psalmist accordingly mitigates the sadness of present evils by administering seasonable consolation, that God’s people, when oppressed by troubles, might look forward with hope to the glorious deliverance which was yet unseen. The sum of the passage is — that God, who had fixed his love upon his chosen people, could not possibly abandon them to such miseries as they now suffered under.

## <19E905>PSALM 149:5-9

**5.** The merciful shall rejoice in glory; they shall shout for joy upon their couches. <span style="color:#800000">fe294</span> 6. The high praises of God are in their throat  <span style="color:#800000">fe295</span> and a two-edged sword is in their hand: 7. To execute vengeance upon the nations, castigations upon the peoples: 8. To bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with iron fetters: 9. To execute upon them the judgment written: this honor is to all his merciful ones. Hallelujah.

<!-- PAGE 842 -->
**5.** <span style="color:#800000">*They shall rejoice.*</span> In making mention here of joy, jubilee, and the high praises of God, he shows still more clearly from the effects which it would produce, that he does not speak of a common benefit of God; for had not the deliverance of the people been of a remarkable kind, there would have been no occasion for such joy, and even triumph. And by these expressions he intimates that the people would not be brought back from exile to be immediately dispersed again, but to flourish in the enjoyment of every species of blessing. He on this account makes mention of *couches,* teaching them to expect daily rest under the divine protection. He declares that they would be furnished with arms and power, not only to ward off enemies, but to put them to flight on every side, so as to reduce to subjection kings and nations which formerly ruled over them. By <span style="color:#800000">*swords of a double-mouth*</span>, or <span style="color:#800000">*two-edged*</span>, are meant such as cut on both sides, for at that time swords had but one edge.

**7.** <span style="color:#800000">*To execute vengeance,*</span> etc. Both during their exile and after their return from it, this might seem to be altogether incredible. Nor did it take place before the advent of Christ; for though the Machabaei and their posterity reduced the neighboring nations to subjection, this was but a faint prelude and earnest to direct the thoughts of the Lord’s people to what was approaching. But as Haggai prophesied that the glory of the second Temple would be greater than of the first, so here there is promised a more prosperous state than had ever existed. (Haggai 2:9.) Reduced as the Jews were in numbers, and low as was the state of things among them, the Psalmist announces to all nations which opposed and troubled them, that they would have the ascendancy. As they were yet tributary, and dwelt at Jerusalem only by sufferance, they were called to exercise faith in a promise which, to the judgment of sense, might appear visionary, and to raise their thoughts to the infinite power of God, which triumphs over all worldly obstacles. The vengeance spoken of is such as the Israelites would take, not under the influence of private resentment, but by commandment of God; and this we mention that none may infer that they are allowed to take vengeance for personal injuries.

<!-- PAGE 843 -->
The next verse, where mention is made of <span style="color:#800000">*kings*</span> and <span style="color:#800000">*nobles*</span>, is an amplification; for had he only spoken of peoples and nations, this might have been restricted to the common people and men of low condition. Here is something much greater — that kings and others of noble rank would be dragged to punishment in chains. But it is to be remembered, as I have just hinted, that but a small part of this splendid prospect was realized until Christ appeared; for any small increase of prosperity which the people enjoyed under the Machabaei was not worthy of any consideration, except in so far as by this help God sustained the drooping spirits of the people up to Christ’s advent. Here the prediction of Jacob is to be noticed —

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#000080">“the scepter shall not depart from Judah, until Shiloh come.”</span> <span style="color:#000080">(</span><span style="color:#000080">Genesis 49:10.)</span></p>

But the Machabaei sprung from another tribe. We must, infer, therefore, that the regular order was then interrupted, and that to make the prosperous state of the people to have been based upon their victories, is building a castle in the air. And God would appear designedly to have removed the government from the tribe of Judah, lest this success should intoxicate the minds of his people; for most of them, through pride in these signal victories, overlooked the true and substantial deliverance. As the Psalmist treats here of the perfection of the prosperity of the people, it follows that he refers to the Messiah, that their expectation and desire of him might never cease either in their prosperity or adversity.

<!-- PAGE 844 -->
**9.** <span style="color:#800000">*To perform the judgment,*</span> etc. He qualifies what he had said in the previous verses, in which he might have appeared to arm the Lord’s people for deeds of warlike cruelty. At first sight it might appear strange, that they who were called the merciful ones of God, should be sent out with drawn swords to commit slaughter, and pour out human blood; for what evidence was here of mercy? But when God himself is the author of the vengeance taken, it is just judgment, not cruelty. When mention is made of the <span style="color:#800000">*judgment written*</span>, the Psalmist reminds the Jews that they were called to liberty by command of God — to that liberty which had been unjustly wrested from them by’ foreigners and tyrants, and that they could not be blamed for executing judgment written. Any exposition of the passage is faulty which does not proceed upon this as being the Psalmist’s design, that he would have the Jews to consider the divine mandate, not to proceed under the influence of private resentment, and to throw a rein over passion; saying upon the matter, that God’s children may not execute vengeance but when called to it, there being an end of all moderation when men yield themselves up to the impulse of their own spirits. Another question might arise here by way of objection. Christ is said to have come without crying or lifting up his voice, that he might not break the bruised reed, (Matthew 12:20,) and he inculcates the same character upon his followers. The answer is obvious, that Christ is also armed with an iron scepter, by which to bruise the rebellious, and is elsewhere described as stained with blood, as slaying his enemies on every side, and not being wearied with the slaughter of them. (Isaiah 63:2.) Nor is it surprising, considering the obstinacy which universally prevails in the world, that the mercy which is treated with such indignity should be converted into severity. Now the doctrine laid down in the passage admits of being rightly applied to our practice, in this way, that what is here said of the two-edged sword, applies more especially to the Jews, and not properly to us, who have not a power of this kind permitted; except, indeed, that rulers and magistrates are vested by God with the sword to punish all manner of violence; but this is something peculiar to their office. <span style="color:#800000">fe296</span> As to the Church collective, the sword now put into our hand is of another kind, that of the word and spirit, that we may slay for a sacrifice to God those who formerly were enemies, or again deliver them over to everlasting destruction unless they repent. (Ephesians 6:17.) For what Isaiah predicted of Christ extends to all who are his members*, —*

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#000080">“He shall smite the wicked with the word of his mouth,</span> <span style="color:#000080">and shall slay them with the breath of his lips.”</span> <span style="color:#000080">(</span><span style="color:#000080">Isaiah 11:4.)</span></p>

If believers quietly confine themselves within these limits of their calling, they will find that the promise of vengeance upon their enemies has not been given in vain. For when God calls us, as I have said above, to judgment written, he puts a restraint both upon our spirits and actions, so as that we must not attempt what he has not commanded. When it is said, in the close of the verse, that <span style="color:#800000">*this honor is to all the merciful ones of God,*</span> he not only exhorts to the practice of piety, but gives us a support for our encouragement, lest we should think that we might be losers by exercising mercy and patience, as most men give vent to fury and rage, under the idea that the only way to defend their life is by showing the savageness of wolves. Although God’s people, therefore, have nothing of the strength of the giant, and will not move a finger without divine permission, ‘and have a calm spirit, the Psalmist declares, that they have an honorable and splendid issue out of all their troubles.

# PSALM 150

The argument of this Psalm is the same with that of the former.

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*Hallelujah.*</span></p>

## <19FE001>PSALM 150:1-6

**1.** Praise God in his sanctuary : praise him in the firmament of his power. 2. Praise him in, his might; praise him for the plenitude of his greatness. 3. Praise him with sound of trumpet, <span style="color:#800000">fe297</span> praise him with psaltry and harp. 4. Praise him with timbrel <span style="color:#800000">fe298</span> and pipe, <span style="color:#800000">fe299</span> praise him upon chords, <span style="color:#800000">fe300</span> and the organ. <span style="color:#800000">fe301</span> 5. Praise him upon cymbals of sound, praise him upon cymbals of jubilation <span style="color:#800000">fe302</span> 6. Whatsoever breathes, let it praise God. Hallelujah.

<!-- PAGE 846 -->
**1.** <span style="color:#800000">*Praise God in his sanctuary.*</span> This psalm in general commends the spiritual worship of God, which consists in sacrifices of praise. By the *sanctuary* there is little doubt that heaven is here meant, as is often the case elsewhere. The second clause is exegetical, for the same thing is repeated. But for sanctuary we read <span style="color:#008080">רקיע</span>, *rekia,* that is, *the expanse of heaven,* to which is added the epithet of <span style="color:#800000">*power*</span>, because there we have a proof of the matchless power of God, so that we cannot look to the heavens without being lost in admiration. As to the interpretation which some give — Praise God, ye angels who inhabit the heavens, and ye men who dwell under the firmament, it is forced and unnatural; for the Psalmist, in order to awaken men who grow languid in God’s praises, bids them lift their eyes towards the heavenly sanctuary. That the majesty of God may be duly reverenced, the Psalmist represents him as presiding on his throne in the heavens; and he enlarges upon the same truth in the second verse, celebrating his power and his greatness, which he had brought under our notice in the heavens, which are a mirror in which they may be seen. If we would have our minds kindled, then, to engage in this religious service, let us meditate upon his power and greatness, which will speedily dispel all such insensibility. Though our minds can never take in this immensity, the mere taste of it will deeply affect us. And God will not reject such praises as we offer according to our capacity.

**3.** <span style="color:#800000">*Praise him with sound of trumpet.*</span> I do not insist upon the words in the Hebrew signifying the musical instruments; only let the reader remember that sundry different kinds are here mentioned, which were in use under the legal economy, the more forcibly to teach the children of God that they cannot apply themselves too diligently to the praises of God — as if he would enjoin them strenuously to bring to this service all their powers, and devote themselves wholly to it. Nor was it without reason that God under the law enjoined this multiplicity of songs, that he might lead men away from those vain and corrupt pleasures to which they are excessively addicted, to a holy and profitable joy. Our corrupt nature indulges in extraordinary liberties, many devising methods of gratification which are preposterous, while their highest satisfaction lies in suppressing all thoughts of God. This perverse disposition could only be corrected in the way of God’s retaining a weak and ignorant people under many restraints, and constant exercises. The Psalmist, therefore, in exhorting believers to pour forth all their joy in the praises of God, enumerates, one upon another, all the musical instruments which were then in use, and reminds them that they ought all to be consecrated to the worship of God.

<!-- PAGE 847 -->
**6.** <span style="color:#800000">*Whatever breathes, etc*</span>. As the word <span style="color:#008080">נשמה</span>, *neshamah,* means *breath,* or *blowing,* and whatever is animate, or breathes, the words may be extended to every kind of living creatures, as we have seen in the preceding psalms that the declaration of God’s praises is assigned even to things wanting intelligence. But as men exclusively are often meant under the name of “flesh,” so we may very well suppose that the words have reference here to men, who, although they have vital breath in common with the brute creation, obtain by way of distinction the name of breathing, as of living creatures. I am led to think this for the following reason: As yet the Psalmist has addressed himself in his exhortations to the people who were conversant with the ceremonies under the law, now he turns to men in general, tacitly intimating that a time was coming when the same songs, which were then only heard in Judea, would resound in every quarter of the globe. And in this prediction we have been joined in the same symphony with the Jews, that we may worship God with constant sacrifices of praise, until being gathered into the kingdom of heaven, we sing with elect angels an eternal hallelujah.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 10</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Why, O Jehovah! standest thou afar off? And winkest at seasonable times in trouble?

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> In his pride the ungodly doth persecute the poor; Let them be caught in the devices which they imagine.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> For praise himself doth the ungodly on account of the desire of his own soul; And the violent man blesseth himself: He despiseth Jehovah.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> The ungodly, in the pride of his countenance doth not inquire; All his devices say, “There is not a God.”

<!-- PAGE 857 -->

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Prosperous are his ways at all times; High are thy judgments before him; At all his enemies he puffeth.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> He saith in his heart, “I shall not be moved from generation to generation,” Because he is not in adversity, <span style="color:#800000">7</span> Of cursing his mouth is full, and of deceit, and of malice: Under his tongue are mischief and iniquity.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> He will sit in the ensnaring places of the villages;  In his lurking places will he murder the innocent: His eyes against the poor will take their aim.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> He will lie in wait in secret, as a lion in his den; He will lie in wait to catch the poor; He will catch the poor by drawing him into his net.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> He will crouch low, he will cast himself down; Then shall fall by his strengths an army of the afflicted.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> He hath said in his heart, “Forgotten it hath God; “He hideth his face, that he may not see it for ever.”

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Arise, O Jehovah, God! lift up thy hand: Do not forget the poor.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Why do the wicked despise God? He saith in his heart, “Thou wilt not require it.”

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> Thou hast seen *it*; For mischief and oppression thou considerest, That thou mayest take them into thy own hand: Upon thee shall the poor leave; To the orphan thou wilt be an helper.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> Break thou the arm of the wicked and the evil man; Thou shalt seek his wickedness, and shalt not find it.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> Jehovah is King for ever and ever; Perished are the heathen out of his land.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> The desire of the needy thou hast heard, O Jehovah! Thou wilt direct their heart; Hear shall thine car:

<!-- PAGE 858 -->

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> That thou mayest judge the fatherless and the poor, That the man *who* is of earth may terrify no more.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 11</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the chief Musician. A Psalm of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> In Jehovah do I put my trust: How then say ye to my soul, “Flee ye into your mountain as a bird? “ <span style="color:#800000">2</span> Surely behold! the ungodly shall bend the bow, They have made ready their arrows upon the string, shoot in secret at the upright in heart.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Truly, the foundations are destroyed: The righteous, what hath he done?

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Jehovah is in the palace of his holiness; Jehovah in heaven *hath* his throne; His eyes behold, his eyelids consider the children of men.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Jehovah will approve the righteous man; But the ungodly and him who loveth iniquity, hate doth his soul.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> He will rain upon the ungodly snares, Fire and brimstone, and a storm of whirlwinds: This is the portion of their cup.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> For the righteous Jehovah loveth righteousness; His countenance approveth the upright.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 12</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician upon the Eighth. A Psalm of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Save me, O Jehovah! for failed hath the merciful man, For wasted away are the faithful from among the children of men.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Deceit doth every one speak with his neighbor; With lips of flatteries, with a double heart do they speak.

<!-- PAGE 859 -->

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Let Jehovah cut off all lips of flatteries, The tongue that great things doth speak:

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Those who have said, “By our tongues we will be strengthened; “Our lips are our own; who is lord over us?”

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> “Because of the spoiling of the needy, “Because of the groaning of the poor, “Now will I arise,” say will Jehovah, “I will set in safety him for whom *the wicked man* layeth snares.”

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> The words of Jehovah are pure words; Silver melted in an excellent crucible of earth, purified seven times.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Thou, O Jehovah! wilt keep them; Thou wilt preserve him from this generation for ever.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> On every side the ungodly walk; When they are exalted, reproach is to the children of men.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 13</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the chief Musician. A Psalm of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> How long, O Jehovah! wilt thou forget me for ever? How long wilt thou hide thy face from me?

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> How long shall I take counsel in my soul? And have sorrow in my heart daily? How long exalted shall be my enemy over me?

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Look upon me, answer me, O Jehovah, my God! Enlighten my eyes, lest I sleep in death;

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Lest my enemy say, “I have prevailed against him; “ And those who afflict me rejoice if I should fall.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> But as for me, in thy goodness I trust; Exult shall my heart in thy salvation. I will sing to the Lord because he hath dealt bountifully with me.

<!-- PAGE 860 -->

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 14</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. A Psalm Of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> The fool hath said in his heart, “There is no God;” They have corrupted [*all good order*,] they have done abominable work. There is none that doeth good.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Jehovah from heaven looked down Upon the children of men, To see whether there were any that did understand, And seek after God.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Every one of them hath gone aside, Together putrid have they become: There is none that doeth good, not even one.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Have they no knowledge all these workers of iniquity? Who eat up my people as they eat bread. Upon the Lord they do not call.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> There did they tremble with fear, For God is in the generation of the righteous.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">6</span> The counsel of the poor ye deride, Because Jehovah is his hope.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Who shall give from Zion salvation to Israel? When turn back shall Jehovah the captivity of his people,  Rejoice shall Jacob, and exult shall Israel.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 15</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Psalm of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> O Jehovah! who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? Who shall rest in the mountain of thy holiness?

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> He who walketh in integrity and doeth righteousness, And who speaketh truth in his heart, <span style="color:#800000">3</span> He who detracteth not with his tongue, Who doeth not to his companion evil, And a calumnious report doth not raise up against his neighbor.

<!-- PAGE 861 -->

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Despised in his eyes is the off cast; But those who fear the Lord he honoreth; When he hath sworn to his own hurt he doth not change.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> His money he doth not put out to usury; And a present upon the innocent he doth not accept: He who doeth these things shall not be moved for ever.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 16</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*Michtam. A Psalm Of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Keep me, O God! *For* in thee do I trust.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Thou shalt say to Jehovah, “My Lord thou art; “My well doing *extendeth* not to thee.”

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> To the saints who are on the earth, And to the excellent; all my delight is in them.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Multiplied shall be their sorrows who offer to a stranger; I will not taste their libations of blood, Nor will I take their names in my lips.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Jehovah is the portion of my inheritance, and of my cup; Thou maintainest my lot.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> The lines have fallen to me in pleasant *places*; Yea, an inheritance that is goodly hath fallen to me.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> I will magnify Jehovah, who giveth me counsel; Even in the nights instruct me do my reins.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> I have set Jehovah before me continually; Since he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Therefore glad is my heart, rejoice doth my tongue; Also my flesh dwelleth in confidence.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> For thou wilt not leave my soul in the grave; Nor wilt thou make thy Holy One to see the pit.

<!-- PAGE 862 -->

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Thou wilt make known to me the way of life; Fullness of joy *is* in thy countenance; Pleasures *are* at thy right hand for evermore.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 17</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Prayer of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Hear, O Jehovah! my righteousness; Attend to my cry; Hearken to my prayer, which is not in lips of deceit.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> From the presence of thy countenance let my judgment go forth Let thine eyes behold uprightness.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Thou hast proved my heart; Thou hast visited *it* by night; Thou hast examined *it*, thou shalt not find *any thing in it*; My thought shall not pass beyond my mouth.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> As for the works of men, by the word of thy lips I have taken heed of the ways of the destroyer.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Uphold my steps in thy paths, That my footsteps may not slide.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> I have called upon thee, surely thou wilt hear me, O God! Incline thy ear to me, and hear my speech.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Make marvelous thy mercies, O thou Preserver of those who trust [*in thee*,] From those that exalt themselves against thy right hand.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Keep me as the apple, the daughter of the eye; In the shadow of thy wings hide me, <span style="color:#800000">9</span> From the face of the ungodly who endeavor to destroy me — Of my enemies who in my soul besiege me.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> In their own fat they have enclosed themselves; With their mouth they have spoken haughtily.

<!-- PAGE 863 -->

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> In our steps they have now encompassed me; eyes they have set to east down to the ground.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> He is like a lion, he desireth to seize his prey, And like a lion’s whelp which lurketh in secret places.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Arise, O Jehovah! confront him, lay him prostrate; Deliver my soul from the ungodly man by thy sword <span style="color:#800000">14</span> From men by thy hand, O Jehovah! — From men who are of long duration, Whose portion is in life, Whose belly thou fillets with thy secret, goods: Filled to the full are their children with them, And their residue they leave to their babes.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> As for me in righteousness I shall behold thy face; I shall be satisfied when I shall awake with thy likeness.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 18</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. Of the servant of Jehovah, David, who spake to*</span> <span style="color:#000080">*Jehovah the words of this song, in the day that Jehovah delivered him from*</span> <span style="color:#000080">*the hand of all his enemies, and from the hand of Saul. And he said,*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> I will love thee, O Jehovah! my strength;

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Jehovah my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer; My God, my rock, I will hope in him: My shield and the horn of my salvation, my refuge.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Upon the praised Jehovah will I call; And from my enemies I shall be saved.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Encompassed me had the cords of death. The torrents of ungodliness had affrighted me.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> The cords of the grave had encompassed me; Prevented me had the snares of death.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> In my distress I called upon Jehovah, And to my God I cried: And he heard from his temple my voice, And my cry before him came, [*even*] into his ears.

<!-- PAGE 864 -->

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Then shake and tremble did the earth; And the foundations of the mountains were troubled and shaken, Because he was wroth.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> There ascended smoke out of his nostrils, And fire *proceeding* from his mouth consumed; Coals were kindled by it.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> And he bowed the heavens and descended; And thick darkness *was* under his feet.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> And he rode upon a cherub and flew; And was carried upon the wings of the wind.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> He made darkness his hiding place; Round about him his pavilion was dark waters, And the clouds of the skies.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> At the brightness *which was* before him his clouds passed away, [*There were*] hail-storm, and coals of fire.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> And thunder in the heavens did Jehovah, And the Most High sent forth his voice; [*There were*] hailstorm and coals of fire.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> And he sent out his army and scattered them; And lightnings he multiplied, and put them into confusion.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> And seen were the abysses of the waters, And disclosed were the foundations of the world, At thy rebuke, O Jehovah! At the blast of the breath of thy nostrils.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> He sent from on high, he took me; He drew me from waters great.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> He delivered me from my enemy [*that was*] strong, And from my adversary; Because they were stronger than I.

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> They had prevented me in the day of my calamity; And Jehovah was a support for me.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> And he brought me forth into a wide place; He rescued me because he wished well to me.

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> Rewarded me hath Jehovah according to my righteousness; According to the purity of my hands he hath repaid me;

<!-- PAGE 865 -->

<span style="color:#800000">21</span> Because I have kept the ways of Jehovah, And have not impiously departed from my God;

<span style="color:#800000">22</span> Because all his judgments *I have had* before me, And his statutes I have not removed from me.

<span style="color:#800000">23</span> And I have been upright with him, And have kept me from my iniquity.

<span style="color:#800000">24</span> And repaid me hath Jehovah according to my righteousness According to the purity of my hands before his eyes.

<span style="color:#800000">25</span> With the merciful thou wilt deal mercifully, With a man of uprightness thou wilt show thyself upright.

<span style="color:#800000">26</span> With the pure thou wilt be pure, And with the perverse thou wilt deal perversely.

<span style="color:#800000">27</span> For thou the afflicted people wilt save, And the haughty eyes thou wilt east down.

<span style="color:#800000">28</span> For thou shalt light my lamp, O Jehovah! My God shall enlighten my darkness.

<span style="color:#800000">29</span> For by thee I shall break through the wedge of a troop, And by my God I shall leap over a wall.

<span style="color:#800000">30</span> As for God perfect is his way; The word of Jehovah [*is*] refined; A shield is He to all who confide in him.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">31</span> For who is God besides Jehovah? And who is strong except our God?</p>

<span style="color:#800000">32</span> It is God who hath girded me with strength, And hath made perfect my way.

<span style="color:#800000">33</span> He maketh my feet like *those* of hinds, And upon my high places he hath set me.

<span style="color:#800000">34</span> He traineth my hands to the battle, And broken will be a bow of steel by my arms.

<!-- PAGE 866 -->

<span style="color:#800000">35</span> And thou hast given me the shield of thy salvation, And thy right hand hath sustained me, And thy clemency hath increased me.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">36</span> Thou hast enlarged my steps under me, And my ankles shall not totter.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">37</span> I will pursue my enemies and will seize them; Nor will I return until I have consumed them.

<span style="color:#800000">38</span> I have afflicted them, and they were not able to rise; They have fallen under my feet.

<span style="color:#800000">39</span> Thou hast girded me with might for the battle; Thou hast bowed down my enemies under me.

<span style="color:#800000">40</span> And of my enemies thou hast given me the neck, And [*as for*] my haters I will destroy them.

<span style="color:#800000">41</span> They shall cry aloud, and *there shall be* no Savior *for them*; To Jehovah, but he shall not answer them.

<span style="color:#800000">42</span> And I will bruise them to powder as dust before the wind; As the mire of the streets I will tread upon them.

<span style="color:#800000">43</span> Thou shalt deliver me from the contentions of the people; Thou shalt make me head of the nations; A people whom I have not known shall serve me.

<span style="color:#800000">44</span> At the hearing of the ear they shall obey me; The children of strangers shall lie to me;

<span style="color:#800000">45</span> The children of strangers shall lose courage, And tremble from within their places of concealment.

<span style="color:#800000">46</span> Let Jehovah live and blessed *be* my strength, And let the God of my salvation be exalted:

<span style="color:#800000">47</span> The God who giveth vengeance for me, And subdueth peoples under me.

<!-- PAGE 867 -->

<span style="color:#800000">48</span> My deliverer from my enemies: Yea, from those who had risen up against me thou hast lifted me up: From the man of violence thou hast rescued me.

<span style="color:#800000">49</span> Therefore will I praise thee, O Jehovah! among the Gentiles, And to thy name will I sing.

<span style="color:#800000">50</span> Who worketh great deliverances for his king, And showeth mercy to his anointed, [even τό David, And to his seed for ever.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 19</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> The heavens recount the glory of God; And the works of his hands proclaim doth the expanse.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Day unto day poureth forth speech; And night unto night publisheth knowledge.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> There is no speech and no language, Where is not heard their voice.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Through all the earth hath gone forth their writing, And to the extremity of the world their words: For the sun he hath set a tabernacle in them, <span style="color:#800000">5</span> And he as a bridegroom goeth forth from his chamber; He exulteth as a strong man to run *his* course.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> From *one* extremity of the heavens *is* his going forth, And his circuit to the utmost limits thereof, And no *person* is hidden from his heat.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> The law of the Lord is perfect, restoring the soul; The testimony of Jehovah is faithful, instructing in wisdom the babes;

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> The statutes of Jehovah *are* right, rejoicing the heart; The commandment of the Lord *is* pure, enlightening the eyes;

<!-- PAGE 868 -->

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> The fear of Jehovah is clean, enduring for ever; The judgments of Jehovah are truth, they are justified together.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> More desirable [*are they*] than gold, and much fine gold; And sweeter than honey, and the dropping of honeycombs.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Moreover, thy servant is made circumspect by them; And in their observance the reward *is* great.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> His errors who can understand? From my hidden *sins* cleanse thou me.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Likewise from presumptuous sins restrain thou thy servant, That they may not have dominion over me; Then upright shall I be and clean from much wickedness.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart be acceptable Before thee, O Jehovah! my strength and my Redeemer.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 20</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. A Psalm Of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> May Jehovah hear thee in the day of trouble!

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> May he send help to thee from the sanctuary! And out of Zion sustain thee!

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> May he be mindful of all thy offerings! And thy holocaust may he make flit! Selah.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">4</span> May he give to thee according to thy heart! And all thy counsel may he fulfill!</p>

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> That we may exult in thy salvation, And in the name of our God erect a banner, When Jehovah shall fulfill all thy petitions.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Now I have known that Jehovah hath saved his anointed; He will hear him from the heavens of his sanctuary, In the mightiness of the salvation of his right hand.

<!-- PAGE 869 -->

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Some *trust* in chariots, and some in horses; But the name of Jehovah our God we will remember.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">8</span> They are bowed down and fallen; But we are risen up and stand erect.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> O Jehovah! do thou save; Let the King hear us in the day that we call upon him.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 21</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. A Psalm Of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> O Jehovah! in thy strength rejoice shall the king, And in thy salvation how greatly shall he exult!

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> The desire of his heart thou hast given him, And what he uttered with his lips, thou hast not denied *him*. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> For thou shalt prevent him with blessings of good; Thou shalt place upon his head a crown of gold.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Life he asked from thee; Thou hast given him length of days for ever and ever.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Great *is* his glory in thy salvation: Splendor and beauty thou hast put upon him.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> For thou hast set him [*to be*] blessings for ever: Thou hast gladdened him with joy before thy countenance.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> For the king trusteth in Jehovah; And through the goodness of the Most High, he shall not be moved <span style="color:#800000">8</span> Find out shall thy hand all thy enemies; Thy right hand shall find out thy haters.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Thou shalt put them as in a furnace of fire in the time of thy wrath, O Jehova! In his wrath he shall overwhelm them, And consume them shall the fire.

<!-- PAGE 870 -->

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> Their fruit from the earth thou wilt destroy, And their seed from among the sons of men. 1l. For they have spread out against thee evil; They have devised against thee a stratagem which they could not accomplish.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> For thou wilt set them as a butt; On thy strings thou shalt make ready *thy arrows* against their faces.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Be thou exalted, O Jehovah! in thy strength, *Then* we will sing and celebrate in psalms thy power.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 22</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. Upon the hind of the morning. A Psalm Of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> My God! my God! why hast thou forsaken me? [*Why art thou*] far from my help, from the words of my roaring?

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> O my God! I cry by day, and thou dost not hear: And in the night, and am not silent.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Yet thou art holy, Inhabiting the praises of Israel.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> In thee trust did our fathers: They trusted, and thou didst deliver them.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> To thee they cried, and were saved: In thee they trusted, and were not put to shame.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> But I *am* a worm, and not a man; The reproach of men, and despised of the people.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> All who see me scoff at me: They thrust out the lip, they shake the head.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> “He hath devolved,” *say they*, “upon Jehovah, *his* cause, let him rescue him, “Let him deliver him, since he hath a favor for him.”

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Surely it is thou who didst take me out of the womb, Causing me to confide upon the breasts of my mother.

<!-- PAGE 871 -->

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> Upon thee I was cast from the womb: From the belly of my mother my God art thou.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Depart not far from me, for trouble is near, For there is no helper.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Encompassed me have bulls [*that are*] strong, The bulls of Bashan have beset me.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">13</span> They have opened upon me their mouth, As a lion ravening and roaring.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> Like water I have flowed, <span style="color:#800000">ff66</span> And disjointed have been  <span style="color:#800000">ff67</span> all my bones: My heart hath been  <span style="color:#800000">ff68</span> like wax, It hath been  <span style="color:#800000">ff69</span>

<p style="margin-left:2em;" markdown="1">melted in the midst of my bowels.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> Dried up as a potsherd hath been  <span style="color:#800000">ff70</span> my strength, And my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; And to the dust of death thou hast brought me.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> For encompassed me have dogs; The assembly of the wicked have surrounded me: They have pierced my hands and my feet.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> I will count all my bones; As for them they look and gaze upon me.

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> They divide my garments among them; Upon my vesture they cast the lot.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> And thou, O Jehovah! be not far from me; *Thou who art* my strength, to my aid hasten.

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> Rescue from the sword my soul; From the hand of the dog my only one.

<span style="color:#800000">21</span> Save me from the mouth of the lion, And from the horns of unicorns do thou hear me.

<span style="color:#800000">22</span> I will declare thy name to my brethren; In the midst of the assembly will I praise thee.

<!-- PAGE 872 -->

<span style="color:#800000">23</span> *Saying*, “Ye who fear Jehovah praise him: “All ye the seed of Jacob glorify him: “And stand in awe of him, all ye the seed of Israel.

<span style="color:#800000">24</span> “For he hath not despised nor disdained the poor; “Nor hath he hidden his face from him; “And when he cried to him, he heard him.”

<span style="color:#800000">25</span> From thee shall proceed my praise in the congregation great; My vows will I pay before them that fear him.

<span style="color:#800000">26</span> Eat shall the poor, and be satisfied; They shall praise Jehovah who seek him; Your heart shall live for ever.

<span style="color:#800000">27</span> Remember and turn to Jehovah shall all the ends of the earth; And prostrate themselves before his face shall all the tribes of the Gentiles.

<span style="color:#800000">28</span> For Jehovah’s is the kingdom, That he may have dominion among the Gentiles.

<span style="color:#800000">29</span> Eat and worship shall all the fat ones of the earth: Before his face shall bow all who are going down to the dust; And he who his own soul doth not quicken.

<span style="color:#800000">30</span> *Their* seed shall serve him, It shall be registered to the Lord for a generation.

<span style="color:#800000">31</span> They shall come and shall declare his righteousness, To a people that shall be born, because he hath done [*this*.],

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 23</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Psalm of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Jehovah is my shepherd, therefore I shall not want any thing.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> In pastures of grass he maketh me to lie down; To waters gently flowing he leadeth me.

<!-- PAGE 873 -->

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> My soul he restoreth: He leadeth me by the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Though I should walk in the valley of the shadow of death, I will not fear evil, because thou art with me; Thy staff and thy crook they comfort me.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Thou wilt prepare before me a table in the presence of my persecutors; Thou wilt anoint with oil my head; My cup overfloweth.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, And I shall dwell in the house of Jehovah for a length of days.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 24</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Psalm of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Jehovah’s is the earth, and the fullness thereof; The world, and those who dwell therein.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> For he upon the seas hath founded it, And upon the floods he hath arranged it.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Who shall ascend into the mountain of Jehovah? Who shall stand in the place of his holiness?

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> He who is clean in hands and pure in heart, Who hath not lifted up to vanity his soul, And hath not sworn deceitfully.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> He shall receive blessing from Jehovah, And righteousness from the God of his salvation.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> This is the generation of those who seek him, Of those who seek thy face, O Jacob! Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Lift up, O ye gates! your heads, And be ye lifted up, ye doors everlasting! And enter shall the King of Glory.

<!-- PAGE 874 -->

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Who is this King of Glory? Jehovah strong and mighty, Jehovah mighty in power. <span style="color:#800000">ff71</span> <span style="color:#800000">9</span> Lift up, O ye gates! your heads, Lift up, I say, ye doors everlasting! *And* enter shall the King of Glory.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">10</span> Who is this King of Glory? Jehovah of armies — He is the King of Glory. Selah.</p>

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 25</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*Of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> To thee, O Jehovah! my soul have I lifted up.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> O my God! in thee have I hoped: Let me not be put to shame, Let not my enemies rejoice over me.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Yea none who wait on thee shall be put to shame: They shall be ashamed who deal perfidiously without cause.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">4</span> Thy ways, O Jehovah! make me to know, Thy paths teach thou me.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> Direct me in thy truth, and teach me; For thou art the God of my salvation; For thee I have waited all the day.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Remember thy compassions, O Jehovah! And thy lovingkindnesses; for they have been from everlasting.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> The transgressions of my youth, and my iniquities do not thou remember According to thy clemency remember thou me, For the sake of thy goodness, O Jehovah!

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Good and upright *is* Jehovah, Therefore he will teach sinners in the way.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> He will guide the poor in judgment, And will teach the poor his way.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> All the ways of Jehovah are mercy and truth, To those who keep his covenant and his testimony.

<!-- PAGE 875 -->

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> For the sake of thy name, O Jehovah! Be merciful to my iniquity, for great is it.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Who is the man that feareth Jehovah? He will teach him in the way which he should choose.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> His soul in good shall dwell, And his seed shall inherit the land.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> The counsel of Jehovah is to those who fear him, That he may make known to them his covenant.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> My eyes are continually towards Jehovah, For he will bring out of the net my feet.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> Have respect to me, take pity upon me, For solitary and poor am I.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> The afflictions of my heart are enlarged; Out of my distresses do thou bring me.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">18</span> Behold my affliction and my travail, And take away all my sins.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> Behold my enemies, for they are multiplied; And with a violent hatred they hate me.

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> Guard my soul, and rescue me, That I may not be ashamed; For I have trusted in thee.

<span style="color:#800000">21</span> Let integrity and rectitude preserve me; Because I have waited for thee.

<span style="color:#800000">22</span> Redeem O God! Israel from all his troubles.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 26</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*Of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Judge me, O Jehovah: Because in my integrity I have walked, And in Jehovah have trusted, I shall not stumble.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Prove me, O Jehovah! and try me, Examine my reins and my heart.

<!-- PAGE 876 -->

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">3</span> For thy goodness *is* before my eyes; Therefore I have walked in thy truth.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> I have not sat with men of vanity, And with crafty men I will not go in.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">5</span> I hate the assembly of transgressors, And with the wicked I will not sit.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> I will wash in purity my hands, And will encompass thy altar, O Jehovah!

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> To cause to be heard the voice of praise, And to tell of all thy marvelous deeds.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> O Jehovah! I have loved the habitation of thy house, And the place of the dwelling of thy glory.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">9</span> Gather not with ungodly men, my soul, Nor with men of bloods my life.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> For in their hands *is* maliciousness, And their right hand is full of bribes.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> But as for me in my integrity I will walk: Redeem me, and have mercy upon me.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> My foot hath stood in uprightness: In the congregations will I bless thee, O Jehovah!

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 27</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*Of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Jehovah is my light and my salvation, Whom shall I fear? Jehovah *is* the strength of my life, Of whom shall I be afraid?

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> When approach against me did the wicked, To devour my flesh — My oppressors and my enemies against me — They stumbled and fell.

<!-- PAGE 877 -->

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> If there should encamp against me a camp, My heart shall not fear: If there should rise against me war, In this shall I have confidence.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> One thing have I requested from Jehovah — This will I follow after — That I may dwell in the house of Jehovah all the days of my life, To behold the beauty of Jehovah, To survey his temple.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> For he shall hide me in his pavilion in the day of evil; He shall conceal me in the secret [*recess*] of his tent, Upon a rock he will set me.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> And now he shall exalt my head Above my enemies who surround me: And I will sacrifice in his tabernacle sacrifices of triumph; I will sing and will celebrate in psalms Jehovah.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">7</span> Hear, O Jehovah! my voice with which I cry; Have mercy upon me and answer me.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> To thee my heart hath said, “Seek ye my face; “ Therefore thy face, O Jehovah! will I seek.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Hide not thy face from me; Cast not away in wrath thy servant: My strength thou hast been, do not desert me, And do not forsake me, O God of my salvation!

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> When my father and my mother shall forsake me, Jehovah shall receive me.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Teach me, O Jehovah! thy way, And lead me in the path of rectitude because of my enemies.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Do not deliver me to the desire of my oppressors, For risen up against me have false witnesses, And he who uttereth violence.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Unless I had believed to see the goodness of Jehovah, in the land of the living —.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> Wait thou on Jehovah; Be strong, and he will comfort thy heart, And wait thou on Jehovah.

<!-- PAGE 878 -->

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 28</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*Of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Unto thee, O Jehovah! will I cry; O my strength! hold not thy peace from me Lest if thou shouldst be silent to me, I then become like those who descend into the grave.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Hear the voice of my prayers when I cry to thee, When I lift up my hands to the sanctuary of thy holiness. 3, Draw me not away with ungodly men, And with the workers of iniquity, Who speak peace  <span style="color:#800000">ff72</span> with their neighbors, When in their hearts is malice.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Give them according to their works, And according to the wickedness of their doings: According to the work of their hands give them, Render their reward to them.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Because they do not consider the doing of Jehovah, Nor the work of his hands, Let him destroy them and not build them up.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Blessed *be* Jehovah! For he hath heard the voice of my supplications.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Jehovah *is* my strength and my shield; In him trusted hath my heart, and I have been helped: Therefore exult shall my heart, And with my song will I celebrate him.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Jehovah *is* strength to them, And the strength of the salvations of his Anointed *is* He.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Save thy people, and bless thy inheritance; Feed them and exalt them for ever.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 29</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Psalm of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Ascribe to Jehovah: ye sons of the mighty — Ascribe to Jehovah glory and strength.

<!-- PAGE 879 -->

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Ascribe to Jehovah the glory of his name; Worship before Jehovah in the brightness of his sanctuary.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> The voice of Jehovah is upon the waters; The God of glory thundereth; Jehovah is upon the waters great.
