<span style="color:#800000">12</span> The sin of their mouth, the words of their lips: Let them be taken in their pride: of cursing and lying let them speak.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Consume, in thy fury consume them, that they may be no more; And let men know that God ruleth in Jacob, Even to the ends of the earth. Selah. <span style="color:#800000">ff87</span> <span style="color:#800000">14</span> And they will return at evening; They will bark like a dog, And go round about the city.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> They will wander up and down for food; If they be not satisfied they will even stay all night.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> But as for me, I will sing of thy strength, I will praise in the morning thy mercy; For thou hast been a fortress to me, And a refuge in the day of my trouble.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> My strength is with thee, I will sing psalms; For God *is* my fortress, the God of my mercy.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 60</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician upon Shushan Eduth. Michtam of David to teach.*</span> <span style="color:#000080">*When he fought against the Syrians of Mesopotamia and against the Syrians*</span> <span style="color:#000080">*of Zobah; and when Joab, having returned, smote of the Edomites in the*</span> <span style="color:#000080">*Valley of Salt twelve thousand*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> O God! thou hast cast us off, thou hast scattered us; Thou hast been angry, O return to us!

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> To tremble thou hast made the earth; Thou hast caused it to open wide; Heal the breaches thereof for it shaketh.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Thou hast showed to thy people a hard thing, Thou hast made us drunk with the wine of stupefaction.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Thou hast given to those who fear thee a banner, That it may be displayed before *thy* truth. Selah.

<!-- PAGE 920 -->

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> That thy beloved ones may be delivered, Save with thy right hand and hear me.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> God hath spoken in his holiness; I will rejoice: I will divide Shechem, And the valley of Succoth I will measure.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Mine *shall be* Gilead, and mine *shall be* Manasseh; And Ephraim *shall be* the strength of my head; Judah, my lawgiver.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Moab *shall be* the pot for my washing; Over Edom will I cast my shoe; O Palestina! triumph thou over me.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">9</span> Who will bring me into the city fortified? Who will lead me into Edom?</p>

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> Wilt not thou, O God! who hadst cast us off?  [*thou*] O God! [*who*] didst not go forth with our armies?

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Grant us relief from trouble, For vain *is* the help of man.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Through God we shall do valiantly: And he it is who shall tread down our adversaries.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 61</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician upon Neginoth. A Psalm of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Hear, O God! my cry, Attend to my prayer.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> From the end of the earth to thee will I cry, when vexed is my heart: To the rock which is higher than I thou shalt lead me.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> For thou hast been a hope to me, A tower of strength from the face of the enemy.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> I will dwell in thy tabernacle for ever; I will be safe under the covert of thy wings. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> For thou, O God! hast heard my vows: Thou hast given an inheritance to those who fear thy name.

<!-- PAGE 921 -->

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Days upon days to the king thou shalt add, His years *shall be* as many generations.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> He shall dwell for ever in the presence of God: Mercy and truth do thou prepare: thou shalt preserve him.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> So will I sing unto thy name for ever, That I may perform my vows every day.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 62</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician upon Jeduthun. A Psalm of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Nevertheless towards God silent is my soul: From him is my salvation.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Nevertheless he is my reek and my salvation, My fortress: *therefore* I shall not be moved greatly.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> How long will ye continue to lay snares against a man? Ye shall be slain all of you: As an inclining wall shall ye be, and a fence that is shaken.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Yet from his elevation they consult to east him down:  They delight in falsehood: With their mouth they bless, And in their hearts they curse. Selah. Nevertheless towards God be thou silent O my soul: For from him *is* my expectation.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Nevertheless he *only is* my rock, and my salvation: My fortress; I shall not fall.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> In God *is* my salvation and my glory; The rock of my strength; my hope *is* in God.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Hope in him at all times, O ye people! Pour out before his face your hearts: God *is* our hope. Selah.

<!-- PAGE 922 -->
<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Nevertheless vanity are the sons of Adam; A lie the sons of men: When put all together in a balance they are found lighter than vanity itself. <span style="color:#800000">ff88</span> <span style="color:#800000">10</span> Trust not in oppression and robbery; be not vain: [*Upon*] riches if they abound set not your heart.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Once God hath spoken; Twice this I have heard, “That power belongeth to God; “ And to thee, O Lord! *belongeth* mercy; Truly thou wilt render to every man according to his work.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 63</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judea*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> O God! my God art thou; Early will I seek thee: Thirsted for thee hath my soul, Longed for thee hath my flesh, In this land [*that is*] inhospitable and dry, without water.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">2</span> Thus in the sanctuary have I beheld thee, To see thy power and thy glory.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Because better *is* thy mercy than life, My lips shall praise thee.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Thus will I bless thee in my life; In thy name I will lift up my hands.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> As with marrow and farness satisfied shall be my soul, And with lips of rejoicing shall my mouth praise *thee*.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Surely I will remember thee upon my bed; In the watches *of the night* I will meditate upon thee;

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Because thou hast been a help to me: And in the shadow of thy wings I will shout for joy.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Cleaved hath my soul to [*literally after*] thee; Sustain me shall thy right hand.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> And they whilst they seek to destroy my soul, Shall go into the lowest parts of the earth.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> They shall east him down to the edge of the sword: The portion of foxes they shall be.

<!-- PAGE 923 -->

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> But the king shall rejoice in God, And glory shall every one who sweareth by him: For stopped shall be the mouth of those who speak falsehood.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 64</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Hear, O God! my voice in my prayer: From fear of the enemy preserve my life.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Hide me from the counsel of malignant men — From the assembly of tire workers of iniquity.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> For they have sharpened as a sword their tongue; They have directed for their arrow a bitter word.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> To shoot in secret at the innocent man: Suddenly they will shoot and not fear.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> They encourage themselves in an impious action; They talk together of secretly laying snares; They say, “Who shall see them?”

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> They have searched out iniquities, They have accomplished a searching search: And the inward part of each of them and the heart [*is*] deep.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> But God shall shoot at them an arrow; Suddenly shall they be wounded.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> And they shall make their own tongue fall upon themselves, And flee away shall all who see them.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> And see shall all men, and shall declare the work of God, And his doing they shall understand.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> Rejoice shall the righteous in Jehovah, and they shall hope in him; And glory shall all the upright in heart.

<!-- PAGE 924 -->

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 65</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David. A Song*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> For thee waiteth praise, O God! in Zion; And to thee performed shall be the vow.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> O thou who hearest prayer! To thee shall all flesh come.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Words of iniquity  <span style="color:#800000">ff89</span> have prevailed against me: Our crimes thou shalt expiate.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Blessed is he whom thou wilt choose, and cause to approach to thee; He shall dwell in thy courts: We shall be satisfied with the goodness of thy house — Of the sanctuary of thy palace.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Terrible things in righteousness wilt thou answer us, O God of our salvation! The hope of all the ends of the earth, And of the far off places of the sea.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">6</span> Establishing the mountains by his power,  <span style="color:#800000">ff90</span> Being girded with might.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Stilling the noise of the seas, And the noise of their waves, the tumults of the nations.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> And afraid shall be the dwellers in the ends *of the earth* at thy signs; The outgoings of the morning and evening thou shalt make to shout for joy.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Thou hast visited the earth, and watered her; Thou hast abundantly enriched her: The river of God is full of waters: Thou wilt prepare their corn, For so thou hast prepared her.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> Her furrows thou dost saturate, Thou makest the rain to fall into her ridges, With showers thou dost moisten her, Her buddings thou dost bless.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Thou crownest the year with thy beneficence, And thy paths will drop fatness.

<!-- PAGE 925 -->

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> They drop upon the dwellings of the wilderness; And with gladness the hills shall be girded.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Clothed are the pastures with flocks; And the valleys are covered with corn; They shout for joy, they also sing.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 66</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Justice,. A Song of a Psalm*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Shout joyfully to God all the earth, <span style="color:#800000">2</span> Sing the glory of his name, Make glorious his praise.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Say unto God: “How terrible art thou in thy works! “Through the greatness of thy power shall thy enemies feign submission unto thee.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> “All the earth shall worship thee, and shall sing to thee, “They shall hymn thy name.” Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Come ye, and see the works of God: He is terrible in his doing towards the sons of men.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> He turned the sea into dry *land*; Through the river  <span style="color:#800000">ff91</span> they passed on foot; There we were glad in him.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> He ruleth by his might over the world;  <span style="color:#800000">ff92</span> His eyes upon the nations are fixed: The rebels shall not exalt themselves. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Bless, O ye people! our God, And resound the voice of his praise.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Who hath brought our souls into life, And hath not suffered our feet to fall.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> For thou hast proved us, O God! Thou hast tried us as silver is tried:

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Thou hast brought us into the net Thou hast laid restraint upon our loins;

<!-- PAGE 926 -->

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Thou hast made man to ride over our heads; We have come into fire and water; And thou hast brought us into a place of abundance.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> I will come into thy house with burnt-offerings; I will pay thee my vows,

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">14</span> Which my lips have uttered, And my mouth hath spoken in my affliction.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> Burnt-offerings of fat *lambs* I will offer to thee with incense of rams; I will bring bullocks with goats. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> Come, hear, and I will tell all you who fear God, What he hath done for my soul.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">17</span> To him with my mouth I cried, And I have exalted him with my tongue.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> If I have regarded iniquity in my heart, The Lord will not hear me.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> But truly heard me hath God; He hath attended to the voice of my prayer.

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> Blessed be God who hath not turned away my prayer, Nor his mercy from me.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 67</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician on Neginoth. A Psalm [*</span><span style="color:#000080">or</span><span style="color:#000080">*] Song*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> May God have compassion upon us, and bless us; May he cause his countenance to shine upon us. Selah.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">2</span> That thy way may be known upon the earth, Among all nations thy salvation.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Let the peoples praise thee, O God! Let all the peoples celebrate thee.

<!-- PAGE 927 -->

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Let the peoples rejoice and exult, For he shall judge the peoples with rectitude, And the nations upon earth thou shalt guide. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Let the peoples celebrate thee, O God! Let all the peoples celebrate thee:

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">6</span> The earth hath given *her* increase; God [*even*] our own God will bless us.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> God will bless us; And fear him shall all the ends of the earth.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 68</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. A Psalm [ορ Song of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Arise shall God: scattered shall be his enemies; And flee from before his face shall those who hate him.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> As smoke is driven away thou shalt drive them away; As wax melteth before the fire, perish shall the ungodly from before the face of God.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">3</span> But the righteous shall rejoice, They shell exult before God, And leap for joy.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Sing ye unto God, sing psalms to his name; Exalt him who rideth upon the clouds whose name is Jah, And exult before him.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> The father of the orphans, and the judge of the widows, *Is* God in the habitation of his holiness.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> God who causeth the solitary to dwell in a family, Who bringeth forth those who are bound with chains: But rebels shall dwell in a dry land.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> O God! when thou well test forth before thy people, When thou marchedst through the wilderness; Selah:

<!-- PAGE 928 -->

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> The earth was moved, Also the heavens dropped at the presence of this God: Sinai at the presence of God, the God of Israel.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> A liberal rain thou shalt make to fall, O God! upon thy inheritance, And when it is weary thou refreshest it.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> Thy congregation shall dwell therein: Thou wilt provide in thy goodness for the poor, O God!

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> The Lord shall give the word To the women who announce the great army.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Kings of armies shall flee — shall flee; And she who dwelleth within the house shall divide the spoils.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Though ye should lie among the pots, *in the ashes*, *Yet shall ye be as* the wings of the dove covered with silver, And *which* behind is *as* fine yellow gold.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> When the Almighty scattered kings in it, It was white in Salmon.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> The mountain of God, the mountain of Bashan, The mountain of heights, the mountain of Bashan.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> Why leap ye, ye mountains of heights? The mountain in which it hath pleased God to dwell: Yea dwell *in it* will Jehovah for ever.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> The chariots of God [*are*] twenty thousand thousands of angels: The Lord *is* among them, In the sanctuary as in Sinai.

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> Thou hast ascended on high; Thou hast led captive captivity; Thou hast received gifts among men; Yea even [*among*] rebels, That Jehovah God might dwell *in the midst of his people*.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> Blessed *be* God day by day: *This* God will load us with deliverances. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> Our God *is* the God of salvations; And to Jehovah Lord *belong* the issues of death.

<!-- PAGE 929 -->

<span style="color:#800000">21</span> Surely God shall wound the head of his enemies, The crown of the hair of him who walketh in his wickedness.

<span style="color:#800000">22</span> The Lord hath said: “From Bashan I will bring back; “I will bring back from the depths of the sea:

<span style="color:#800000">23</span> “That thy foot may be stained with blood, “The tongue of thy dogs even in that of thy enemies.”

<span style="color:#800000">24</span> They have seen thy goings, O God!— The goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary.

<span style="color:#800000">25</span> Before went the singers; [*Then*] followed the players on instruments; In the midst [*were*] the damsels striking the timbrels.

<span style="color:#800000">26</span> In the congregations bless ye God, [*Even*] the Lord, *ye who* are of the fountain of Israel!

<span style="color:#800000">27</span> There *was* little Benjamin their ruler, The princes of Judah in their assembly, The princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphthali.

<span style="color:#800000">28</span> Commanded hath thy God thy strength; Strengthen, O God! what thou hast wrought in us.

<span style="color:#800000">29</span> From thy temple upon Jerusalem To thee shall kings bring presents.

<span style="color:#800000">30</span> Destroy the company of spearmen, The assembly of bulls, with the calves of the peoples, Treading with their feet upon pieces of silver: Scatter thou the peoples that in wars delight.

<span style="color:#800000">31</span> Princes shall come out of Egypt; Ethiopia shall speedily stretch forth her hands to God.

<span style="color:#800000">32</span> O ye kingdoms of the earth! sing unto God: Sing psalms to the Lord. Selah.

<!-- PAGE 930 -->
<span style="color:#800000">33</span> To him who rideth upon the heavens of heavens *which are* of old: Lo! he shall send forth in his voice a voice of strength, <span style="color:#800000">34</span> Ascribe ye strength to God over Israel; His majesty and his strength [*are*] in the clouds.

<span style="color:#800000">35</span> Terrible art thou, O God! out of thy holy places: The God of Israel himself shall give strength and might to his people. Blessed *be* God!

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 69</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician upon Shoshannim. Of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Save me, O God! For entered have the waters even to my soul.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> I am sunk into deep mire where there is no standing place; I am come into the depths of waters, And the floods of water have overflowed me.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> I am weary with crying, Hoarse is my throat become therewith; Failed have my eyes with waiting for my God.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> More in number than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause: Increased are those who desire to destroy me, [*even*] my lying adversaries: That which I took not by violence, then I restored it.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">5</span> O God! thou knowest my foolishness, And my faults from thee are not hidden.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Let not those be ashamed in me that wait for thee, O Lord, Jehovah of armies! Let not those be put to shame in me who seek thee, O God of Israel!

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> For on thy account I have suffered reproach; Shame hath covered my face.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> A stranger I have been to my brethren, And an alien I am become to the children of my mother.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> For the zeal of thy house hath eaten me up; And the reproaches of those who reproached thee have fallen upon me.

<!-- PAGE 931 -->

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">10</span> And I wept, my soul fasted; And that was for a reproach to me.</p>

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">11</span> And I made my garment sackcloth; And I was to them for a jest.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Defame me do those who sit in the gate; And *I am* the songs of those who drink intoxicating liquor.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> But as for me my prayer [*is*] to thee, O Jehovah! *In the* time of *thy* favor, O God! In the multitude of thy mercy answer me, In the truth of thy salvation.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> Rescue me from the mire that I may not sink; That I may be delivered from my adversaries, And from the depths of waters.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> Let not the flood of waters overflow me; And let not the deep swallow me up; And let not the pit dose its mouth upon me.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> Answer me, O Jehovah! for good *is* thy mercy: In the multitude of thy compassions look upon me.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> And hide not thy face from thy servant, for I am afflicted: Hasten! answer me!

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> Draw near to my soul, redeem it: On account of my adversaries deliver me.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion, and my ignominy: Before thee *are* all my adversaries.

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> Reproach hath broken my heart, and I am afflicted; And I looked for some one to show compassion, but there was none; For comforters, but I found *them* not.

<span style="color:#800000">21</span> And they put into my meat gall, And in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.

<span style="color:#800000">22</span> Let their table be before them for a snare; And their prosperity for a net;

<span style="color:#800000">23</span> Darkened let be their eyes, that they may not see; And cause their loins continually to tremble.

<!-- PAGE 932 -->

<span style="color:#800000">24</span> Pour out upon them thy wrath; And let the fury of thy indignation take hold of them.

<span style="color:#800000">25</span> Let their palace be desolate; In their tents let there not be a dweller.

<span style="color:#800000">26</span> For him whom thou hast smitten they have persecuted; And to the grief of those whom thou hast wounded they have added.

<span style="color:#800000">27</span> Add iniquity to their iniquity; And let them not enter into thy righteousness.

<span style="color:#800000">28</span> Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; And with the righteous let them not be written.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">29</span> But as for me I am poor and sorrowful: Thy salvation shall exalt me.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">30</span> I will praise the name of God in a song, And I will magnify him with thanksgiving.

<span style="color:#800000">31</span> And this will please Jehovah More than a young bullock that hath horns and hoofs.

<span style="color:#800000">32</span> Seen it have the afflicted, And they shall rejoice at it who seek God; And live shall your heart.

<span style="color:#800000">33</span> For hearkened hath Jehovah to the afflicted; And his prisoners he hath not despised.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">34</span> Praise him let heaven and earth; The seas and whatever creepeth in them.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">35</span> For God will save Zion, And will build the cities of Judah; And they shall dwell there, And possess it by inheritance.

<span style="color:#800000">36</span> And the seed of his servants shall inherit it; And they who love his name shall dwell in it.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 70</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. Of David. To call to remembrance*</span></p>

<!-- PAGE 933 -->

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> O God! to deliver me, O Jehovah! to my aid, hasten.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Let those be ashamed and confounded who seek after my soul; Let those be turned backward and put to confusion who desire my hurt.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Let those be destroyed for a reward of their shame, Who say to me, “Aha! Aha!”

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Exult and rejoice in thee let all who seek thee; And let those say, “For ever may God be magnified” — Those who love thy salvation.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> But as for me I am poor and needy: O God! hasten to me: My help and my deliverer art thou: O Jehovah! delay not.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 71</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> In thee, O Jehovah! do I put my trust, Let me not be put to shame for ever.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> In thy righteousness deliver me, and rescue me; Incline to me thy ear, and save me.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Be thou to me for a rock of strength, Into which I may enter at all times: Thou hast given commandment to save me; For my tower and my fortress art thou.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> O my God! deliver me from the hand of the ungodly man, — From the hand of the wicked and violent men.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> For thou art my expectation, O Lord Jehovah! My trust from my youth.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Upon thee have I been sustained from the womb; Out of my mother’s bowels thou art he who took me: Of thee is my praise continually.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> As a prodigy I have been to the great ones, And yet thou art my strong confidence.

<!-- PAGE 934 -->

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Filled shall be my mouth with thy praise, Daily with thy glory.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Cast me not off in the time of my old age: In the declining of my strength forsake me not.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> For my enemies have spoken concerning me, And those who watch for my soul have consulted together, <span style="color:#800000">11</span> Saying, “God hath forsaken him; “Follow after him, and ye shall take him; “For there is none to deliver *him*.”

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> O God! be not far from me: O my God! to my aid hasten.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Let those be put to shame, let those fail who are the adversaries of my soul: Let those be covered with reproach mid shame who seek my hurt.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> But as for me continually will I hope, And will add to all thy praise.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> My mouth shall tell of thy righteousness, Daily of thy salvation; For I know not the number *thereof*.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> I will go in the strength of the Lord Jehovah! I will remember thy righteousness alone.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> O God! thou hast taught me from my youth; And unto this time will I announce thy wonders.

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> And therefore  <span style="color:#800000">ff93</span> in old age and gray hairs, O God! forsake me not, Until I have declared thy strength to the generation, To all who are to come thy might.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> And thy righteousness, O God! is very high: For thou hast done great things: O God! who is like to thee?

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> Thou hast made me to see troubles many and grievous, *But* being turned thou wilt quicken me, And from the depths of the earth, being turned thou wilt raise me up.

<span style="color:#800000">21</span> Thou wilt multiply my greatness; And being turned thou wilt comfort me.

<!-- PAGE 935 -->

<span style="color:#800000">22</span> Moreover, I, even I, will sing to thee on instruments of music; <span style="color:#800000">ff94</span> For thy truth, O my God! I will sing psalms to thee upon the harp, O Holy One of Israel!

<span style="color:#800000">23</span> Exult shall my lips, when I sing psalms to thee; And my soul which thou hast redeemed.

<span style="color:#800000">24</span> Also my tongue daily shall declare thy righteousness; For they are put to shame, for they are disgraced, who seek my hurt.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 72</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*Of Solomon*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> O God! thy judgments give to the King, And thy righteousness to the son of the King <span style="color:#800000">2</span> He shall judge thy people in righteousness, And thy poor ones in judgment.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Bring forth shall the mountains peace to the people, And the hills in righteousness.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> He shall judge the poor ones of the people; He shall save the children of the afflicted; And shall break in pieces the calumniator.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> They shall fear thee with the sun; And before the moon the generation of generations shall fear thee.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> He shall descend as rain upon the mown grass; As the showers which water the earth.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Flourish in his days shall the righteous; And abundance of peace until there be no more moon.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> And he shall have dominion from sea to sea, And from the river even to the ends of the earth.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Before him shall bow the inhabitants of the desert, And his enemies shall lick the dust.

<!-- PAGE 936 -->

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> The kings of Tarshish and of the isles a present shall bring: The kings of Sheba and Seba a gift shall offer *to him*.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> And all kings shall prostrate themselves before him; All nations shall serve him.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> For he shall deliver the poor who crieth *to him*, And the needy who hath no helper.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> He will have compassion upon the indigent and the poor one, And the souls of the poor ones he will save.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> From fraud and violence he will redeem their souls, And precious shall be their blood in his eyes.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> And he shall live, and there shall be given to him of the gold of Sheba, And prayer shall be made for him continually; Daily shall he be blessed.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> There shall be *sown* an handful of corn in the earth on the top of the mountains; The fruit thereof shall be shaken like [*that*] of Lebanon. And they shall go forth from the city as a plant of the earth.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> His name shall be for ever; In presence of the sun propagated shall be his name: And bless themselves in him shall all nations, And blessed they shall call him.

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> Blessed be Jehovah God! the God of Israel! <span style="color:#800000">ff95</span> Who doeth wonderful things alone.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> And blessed be his glorious name for ever; And let all the earth be filled with his glory. Amen and Amen.

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> Finished are the prayers of David, the son of Jesse.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1">PART THIRD<span style="color:#800000">96</span></p>

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 73</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Psalm of Asaph*</span></p>

<!-- PAGE 937 -->

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Yet God is good to Israel, To those who are right in heart.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">2</span> As for me, wellnigh slipped had my feet, My steps were almost gone:</p>

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">3</span> For I was envious at the foolish, On seeing the prosperity of the ungodly.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> For there are no bands to their death, And vigorous is their strength.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> In the [*common*] trouble of man they are not; And with other men they are not scourged.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Therefore encompass them as a chain doth pride; Covered them hath the raiment of violence.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Their eye projecteth through fatness; They have passed beyond the thoughts of their heart.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> They break forth, and talk wickedly of extortion: From on high do they speak.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> They have set against the heaven their mouth, And their tongue walketh through the earth.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> On this account his people will return hither, And waters of a full cup will be wrung out to them.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">11</span> And they say, “How doth God know? “And is there knowledge in the Most High? “</p>

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Behold these are the ungodly, and [*yet*]. they are in quiet for ever: They heap up riches.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Surely in vain I have purified my heart, And washed every day my hands:

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> And I have been scourged every day, And my chastisement [*has been*] every morning.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> If I have said, “I will speak thus,” Behold! the generation of thy children: I have transgressed.

<!-- PAGE 938 -->

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> And although I applied my mind to know this, A pain fill thing it was in mine eyes, <span style="color:#800000">17</span> Until I entered into the sanctuaries of God, *And* understood their end.

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> Surely in slippery places thou hast set them; Thou shalt east them down into destructions.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> How have they been destroyed as in a moment! They have perished, they have been consumed with terrors.

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> As it were a dream after a man is awakened; O Lord! in awaking, their image thou wilt render contemptible.

<span style="color:#800000">21</span> For in a ferment was my heart, And in my reins I was pierced.

<span style="color:#800000">22</span> And I myself [*was*] foolish and knew not *any thing*; As the beasts have I been before thee.

<span style="color:#800000">23</span> Nevertheless *I have been* continually with thee; Thou hast held my right hand.

<span style="color:#800000">24</span> With thy counsel thou shalt guide me; And at length to glory thou shalt take me.

<span style="color:#800000">25</span> Whom have I in heaven *but thee*? And another with time I have not desired on the earth.

<span style="color:#800000">26</span> Failed have my flesh and my heart; *But* the strength of my heart and my portion *is* God for ever.

<span style="color:#800000">27</span> For lo! those who depart from thee shall perish: Thou hast destroyed every one who goeth a whoring from thee.

<span style="color:#800000">28</span> As for me, to draw near to God is good for me: I have put in the Lord Jehovah my trust, That I may tell of all thy works.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 74</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*An Instruction of Asaph*</span></p>

<!-- PAGE 939 -->

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Wherefore, O God! hast thou cast us off for ever? [*Why*] smoketh thy wrath against the flock of thy pastures?

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Remember thy congregation which thou hast possessed of old; <span style="color:#800000">ff97</span> *Which* thou hast redeemed, the rod of thy inheritance, This Mount Zion in which thou hast dwelt.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Lift up thy strokes to desolations perpetual, Against every enemy who doeth mischief to the sanctuary.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Roared *like lions* have thy adversaries in the midst of thy sanctuaries; They have set up their signs *for* signs.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> He was renowned as doing an excellent work Who lifted up the axes upon the thick trees. <span style="color:#800000">ff98</span> <span style="color:#800000">6</span> And now the carved works thereof together, With the hatchet and with hammers they break in pieces.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> They have set on fire thy sanctuaries; Leveling it with the ground, they have polluted the dwelling-place of thy name.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> They have said in their heart, “Let us destroy them altogether.” They have burned all the tabernacles of God in the land.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Our signs we see not; There is no longer a prophet, Nor is there with us one who knoweth how long! — <span style="color:#800000">10</span> How long, O God! shall the adversary reproach? Shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> How long wilt thou withdraw thy hand, and thy right hand? In the midst, of thy bosom consume them.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> But God *is* my king from the beginning, Working salvations in the midst of the earth.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Thou didst divide  <span style="color:#800000">ff99</span> by thy power the sea; Thou didst break the heads of dragons in the waters.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> Thou didst break the head of the leviathan; Thou gavest him *for* food to *thy* people in the wilderness.

<!-- PAGE 940 -->

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> Thou didst cleave the fountain and the torrent: Thou didst dry up mighty rivers.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> Thine is the day; thine also is the night: Thou hast ordained the light and the sun.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> Thou hast fixed all the boundaries of the earth: The summer and the winter thou hast made.

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> Remember this: the enemy hath reproached Jehovah; And a worthless people hath done despite to thy name.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> Give not to the beast the soul of thy turtle dove: The congregation of thy poor ones forget not for ever.

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> Have regard to *thy* covenant; For filled are the dark places of the earth with the abodes of violence.

<span style="color:#800000">21</span> Let not the afflicted one return ashamed; Let the poor and needy one praise thy name.

<span style="color:#800000">22</span> Arise, O God! plead thy own cause: Remember thy reproach, *which is done thee* by the foolish man daily.

<span style="color:#800000">23</span> Forget not the voice of thy adversaries: The tumult of those who rise up against thee ascendeth continually.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 75</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. Destroy not. A Psalm of Asaph. A song*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> We will celebrate thee, O God! we will celebrate *thee*; And near is thy name: they will declare thy wonders.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> When I shall have taken the congregation, I in uprightness will judge.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Dissolved is the earth, and all the inhabitants thereof: will establish the pillars of it. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> I said to the fools, “Act not foolishly; “ And to the ungodly, “Raise not up the horn.”

<!-- PAGE 941 -->

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Raise not up on high your horn; And speak not with a stiff neck. g. For neither from the east, nor from the west, Nor from the wilderness are exaltations.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> For God is judge: tie bringeth low, and he setteth up.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> For a cup *is* in the hand of Jehovah, and the wine is turbid; It is full of mixture, and he shall pour forth of it. Surely the dregs thereof they shall wring out;. And drink *of it* shall all the wicked of the earth.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> But as for me I will publish for ever, I will sing psalms to the God of Jacob.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> And all the horns of the ungodly I will break; But exalted shall be the horns of the righteous.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 76</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician on Neginoth. A Psalm of Asaph. A Song*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Known in Judah is God; In Israel great is his name.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> And in Salem was his tabernacle, And his dwelling-place in Zion.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> There he broke the arrows of the bow, The shield, and the sword, and the battle. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> More glorious, more terrible *art* thou Than the mountains of prey.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Spoiled were the stout in heart, They slept their sleep: And none of the men of might have found their hands.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> At thy rebuke, O God of Jacob! Cast into a deep sleep were the chariot and the horse.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Thou *art* terrible [*even*] thou; And who shall stand before thy face when thou art angry?

<!-- PAGE 942 -->

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> From the heavens thou hast made judgment to be heard: The earth was afraid and was still,

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">9</span> When God arose to judgment, To save all the meek of the earth. Selah.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> Surely the wrath of men shall praise thee, The remainder of wrath thou wilt restrain.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Vow and pay to Jehovah your God: Let all who are round about him bring a present to the terrible one.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> He will cut off the spirit of princes: *He is* terrible to the kings of the earth.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 77</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician upon Jeduthun. A Psalm of Asaph*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> My voice [*I lifted up*] to God, and I cried; My voice [*I lifted up*] to God, and he heard me.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> In the day of my affliction the Lord I sought: My hand in the night was stretched out and relaxed not; Refuse consolation did my soul.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> I will remember God, and will be disquieted; I will meditate, and oppressed with sorrow shall be my spirit. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Thou hast held the watches of my eyes: I am troubled, and will not speak.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> I have recounted the days of old, The years of ages past.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> I will call to remembrance my song in the night: With my heart I will meditate, And search diligently shall my spirit.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> For ever will the Lord east off? And will he be favorable no more?

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Gone for ever is his mercy? Fail doth his oracle from generation to generation?

<!-- PAGE 943 -->

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Forgotten to be merciful hath God? Hath he shut up in anger his compassions? Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> And I said my disease [*is only for a season*;] The years of the right hand of the Most High [*I will wait for*.] <span style="color:#800000">11</span> I will remember the works of God; Surely I will remember thy wonders from the beginning.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> And I will meditate on all thy works, And on thy doings I will muse.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> O God! in the sanctuary *are* thy ways: What god *is* so great as God?

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> Thou art the God who doest wonders; Thou hast made known among the peoples thy strength.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> Thou hast redeemed by [*thy*] arm thy people, The sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> See thee did the waters, O God! see thee did the waters; They were afraid; also tremble did the deeps.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> The clouds poured out waters; The heavens gave forth a voice: Also thine arrows went abroad.

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> The voice of thy thunder was in the circuit, The lightnings illumined the world; The earth trembled and was shaken.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> In the sea are thy ways, And thy paths in the great waters; And thy footsteps are not known.

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> Thou leadest like sheep thy people By the hand of Moses and Aaron.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 78</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A lesson of Instruction [οφ Asaph*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Give ear, O my people! to my law: Incline your ears to the words of my month.

<!-- PAGE 944 -->

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> I will open in a parable my mouth; I will utter enigmas from ancient Sae.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> What we have heard and known, And our’ fathers have related to us, <span style="color:#800000">4</span> We will not conceal from their children to the generation to come, Recounting the praises of Jehovah and his might, And the wonders which he hath done.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> And he established a testimony in, Jacob, And a law he appointed in Israel; For lie commanded our fathers To make them known to their children;

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> That the generations to come might know them, *That* the children to be born might arise, And declare *them* to their children.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> That they might set in God their hope, And not forget the works of God; But that his commandments they might observe, <span style="color:#800000">8</span> And not be as their fathers, A generation rebellious and provoking; A generation which set not their heart might, And whose spirit was not faithful towards God.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> The children of Ephraim, armed [*and*] shooting with the bow, Were turned back in the day of battle.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> They kept not the covenant of God, And in his law they refused to walk.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> And they forget his works, And the wonders which he had shown them.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> In the sight of their fathers he wrought marvelously; In the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> He divided the sea, and caused them to pass through, And made the waters to stand as an heap.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> And he led them by a cloud in the day; And all the night by the light of fire.

<!-- PAGE 945 -->

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">15</span> He clave the rocks in the wilderness, And made them to drink in great deeps.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> And he brought forth streams from the rock, And made the waters to descend like rivers.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> Yet they continued still to sin against him, To provoke the Most High in the wilderness.

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> And they tempted God in their heart, By asking food for their soul.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> And they spake against God: They said, “Can God prepare a table in the wilderness?”

<span style="color:#800000">20</span> Behold! he smote the reek, and gush out did the waters; And rivers overflowed. “Can he give bread also? “Will he prepare flesh for his people?”

<span style="color:#800000">21</span> Therefore Jehovah heard and was wroth: And a fire was kindled in Jacob: And wrath also ascended against Israel;

<span style="color:#800000">22</span> Because they believed not in God, And trusted not in his salvation.

<span style="color:#800000">23</span> But he had commanded the clouds from above, And the doors of heaven he had opened, <span style="color:#800000">24</span> And had rained down upon them manna for food, And the corn of heaven he had given them:

<span style="color:#800000">25</span> The bread of the mighty ones man had eaten: Meat he had sent them to the full.

<span style="color:#800000">26</span> He caused to blow an east wind in the heavens; And he raised up by his power the south wind.

<span style="color:#800000">27</span> And he rained upon them flesh as dust, And as the sand of the sea leathered fowl;

<span style="color:#800000">28</span> And he caused *it* to fall in the midst of his camp, Round about his tabernacles.

<!-- PAGE 946 -->

<span style="color:#800000">29</span> And they did eat and were filled exceedingly, And their desire he brought to them.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">30</span> They were not estranged from their desire: The meat was still in their mouth,</p>

<span style="color:#800000">31</span> When the wrath of God ascended against them, And slew their fat ones, And brought low the chosen of Israel.

<span style="color:#800000">32</span> In all these *things* they sinned still, And believed not his wonders.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">33</span> And he consumed in vanity their days, And their years in haste.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">34</span> When he slew them, they sought him; They returned, and hastened early to God.

<span style="color:#800000">35</span> And they remembered that God was their Rock, And *that* the Most High God was their Redeemer.

<span style="color:#800000">36</span> And they flattered [*him*] with their mouth, And with their tongue they lied to him:

<span style="color:#800000">37</span> But their heart was not right before him, And they were not faithful in his covenant.

<span style="color:#800000">38</span> Yet he *who is* compassionate expiated their iniquity, And did not destroy them: And he multiplied to turn away his anger, And did not stir up all his indignation.

<span style="color:#800000">39</span> And he remembered that they were flesh; A breath that passeth, and returneth not.

<span style="color:#800000">40</span> How often did they provoke him in the desert, [*And*] grieve him in the wilderness!

<span style="color:#800000">41</span> And they returned and tempted God, And the Holy One of Israel they limited.

<!-- PAGE 947 -->
<span style="color:#800000">42</span> They remembered not his hand In the day that he redeemed them from the oppressor, <span style="color:#800000">43</span> When he set in Egypt his signs, And his miracles in the field of Zoan.

<span style="color:#800000">44</span> When he turned into blood their rivers; And their streams, that they might not drink of them.

<span style="color:#800000">45</span> He sent among them a mixture which devoured them; And the frog which destroyed them.

<span style="color:#800000">46</span> And he gave to the caterpillar their fruit; And their labors to the locusts. <span style="color:#800000">ff100</span> <span style="color:#800000">47</span> And he destroyed with hail their vine, And their wild fig-trees with hailstones.

<span style="color:#800000">48</span> And he gave lip to the hail their cattle, And their flocks to thunderbolts.

<span style="color:#800000">49</span> He sent upon them the fierceness of his wrath, Fury, anger, and affliction, A mission of evil angels.

<span style="color:#800000">50</span> He made a path for his anger: He kept not from death their soul, And their cattle to the pestilence he shut up.

<span style="color:#800000">51</span> And he smote all the firstborn in Egypt: The beginning of [*their*] strength in the tents of Ham.

<span style="color:#800000">52</span> And he made to go forth like sheep his people, And led them like a flock in the wilderness.

<span style="color:#800000">53</span> And he conducted *them* in safety, and they were not afraid: And their enemies cover did the sea.

<span style="color:#800000">54</span> And he brought them to the border of his holiness, This mountain, *which* his right hand acquired.

<span style="color:#800000">55</span> And he expelled from before their face the heathen; And made them to fall into the lot of all inheritance; And caused to dwell in their tents the children of Israel.

<span style="color:#800000">56</span> But they tempted and provoked God Most High, And his testimonies they kept not.

<!-- PAGE 948 -->

<span style="color:#800000">57</span> And they turned back and dealt perfidiously like their fathers: They started aside like a bow that is deceitful.

<span style="color:#800000">58</span> And they provoked him to anger with their high places; And with their graven images they moved him to anger.

<span style="color:#800000">59</span> Hear it did God, and was wroth, And he abhorred exceedingly Israel.

<span style="color:#800000">60</span> And he forsook the habitation of Shiloh, The tabernacle where he dwelt among men.

<span style="color:#800000">61</span> And he gave into captivity his strength, And his beauty into the hand of the enemy.

<span style="color:#800000">62</span> And he shut up to the sword his people, And with his own inheritance was wroth.

<span style="color:#800000">63</span> Their chosen devour did the fire, And their virgins were not applauded.

<span style="color:#800000">64</span> Their priests by the sword did fall; And their widows made no lamentation.

<span style="color:#800000">65</span> But the Lord awoke as one asleep, As a mighty man who crieth out by reason of wine.

<span style="color:#800000">66</span> And he smote his enemies behind; Everlasting disgrace he put upon them.

<span style="color:#800000">67</span> And he rejected the tabernacle of Joseph, And the tribe of Ephraim he chose not:

<span style="color:#800000">68</span> But he chose the tribe of Judah, The mountain of Zion, which lie loved:

<span style="color:#800000">69</span> And built like high places his sanctuary, Like the earth which he hath founded for ever.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">70</span> And he chose David his servant, And took him from the folds of sheep:</p>

<!-- PAGE 949 -->

<span style="color:#800000">71</span> From following the suckling ewes he took him, To feed Jacob his people, And Israel his inheritance:

<span style="color:#800000">72</span> And he fed them in the integrity of his heart, And by the prudence of his hands he guided there.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 79</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Psalm of Asaph*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> O God! come have the heathen into thy inheritance; They have polluted the temple of thy holiness; They have laid Jerusalem in heaps. [fowls of the heavens;

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> They have given the dead bodies of thy servants for food to the fowls of the heavens; The flesh of thy meek ones to the beasts of the earth.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> They have shed their blood like water around Jerusalem: And there was not *one* to bury *them*.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> We have been a reproach to our neighbors; A scorn and a derision to those who are around us.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> How long, O Jehovah! wilt thou be wroth for ever? Burn like fire shall thy jealousy?

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Pour out thy wrath upon the heathen who have not known thee, And upon the kingdoms which upon thy name do not call:

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> For they have devoured Jacob, And his dwelling they have laid waste.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Remember not against us former iniquities: Make haste, let thy compassions prevent us; For we are afflicted exceedingly.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Help us, O God of our salvation! for the glory of thy name; And deliver us, and be merciful to our sins, for the sake of thy name.

<!-- PAGE 950 -->

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> Wherefore should the heathen say, “Where is their God?” Let be made known among the heathen in our sight The vengeance of the blood of thy servants which is shed.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Let the sighing of the prisoner come before thy face: According to the greatness of thy arm, Reserve the children of death:  <span style="color:#800000">ff101</span> <span style="color:#800000">12</span> And recompense our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom, Their reproach with which they have reproached thee, O Jehovah!

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> And we thy people, and the sheep of thy pastures, Will confess to thee for ever; From generation to generation declaring thy praise.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 80</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician upon Shoshannim Eduth. A Psalm of Asaph*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> O Shepherd of Israel, give ear! Who leadest Joseph like a flock; Thou who sittest between the cherubim, shine forth.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Before Ephraim, and Benjamin, and Manasseh, Stir up thy strength, and come for our salvation.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">3</span> Turn us again, O God! and cause to shine thy face, And we shall be safe.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> O Jehovah God of armies! How long wilt thou be incensed against the prayer of thy people?

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Thou hast fed us with bread of tears; And hast given us tears to drink in great measure.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Thou hast made us a strife to our neighbors: And our enemies laugh *at us* among themselves.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> O God of armies! turn us again, And cause to shine thy face upon us, And we shall be safe.

<!-- PAGE 951 -->

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> A vine out of Egypt thou hast brought: Thou hast expelled the heathen, and planted it,.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Thou hast cleansed *the ground* before it: Thou hast rooted its roots, And it hath filled the land.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> Covered were the mountains with its shadow, And its branches *were like* the cedars of God.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> It sent forth its branches to the sea, And to the river its shoots.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Why then hast thou broken down its hedges, So that tear it in pieces do all who pass by the way?

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Wasted it hath the boar out of the forest; And the wild beast of the field hath eaten it up.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> O God of armies! return, I beseech *thee*, Look down from heaven, and behold, And visit this vine, <span style="color:#800000">15</span> And the vineyard which planted hath thy right hand, And [*look*] upon the shoot  <span style="color:#800000">ff102</span> *which* thou hast strengthened for thyself.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> It is burnt with fire; it is cut down; At the rebuke of thy countenance they perish.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> Let thy hand be upon the Man of thy right hand, Upon the son of man whom thou hast strengthened for thyself, <span style="color:#800000">18</span> And we will not go back from thee: Thou shalt quicken us, and upon thy name we will call.

<span style="color:#800000">19</span> O Jehovah, God of armies! turn us again; Cause to shine thy face, And we shall be safe.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 81</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician upon Gittith. Of Asaph*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Exult to God our strength: Shout for joy to the God of Jacob.

<!-- PAGE 952 -->

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Take a song, and bring forth the timbrel, The harp of pleasantness with the nablum.  <span style="color:#800000">ff103</span> <span style="color:#800000">3</span> Sound the trumpet  <span style="color:#800000">ff104</span> at the new moon; At the time appointed on the day of our sacrifice.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> For a statute to Israel *is* this, A judgment to the God of Jacob.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> For a testimony in Joseph he set it, When he went forth over the land of Egypt! A language which I understood not I heard.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> “I removed from the burden his shoulder: “His hands from the pots were removed.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> “In trouble thou didst cry, and I rescued thee: “I answered thee in the secret place of thunder: “I proved thee at the waters of Meribah. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> “Hear, O my people! and I will protest to thee: “O Israel! if thou wilt hearken to me.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">9</span> “Let there not be in thee a strange god: “Neither worship thou a foreign god.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> “I *am* Jehovah thy God, “Who brought thee out of the land of Egypt: “Open wide thy mouth, and I will fill it.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> “But my people hearkened not to my voice, “And Israel would have none of me.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> “And I gave them up to the hardness of their heart: “They shall walk in their own counsels.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> “O if my people had hearkened to me! “*If* Israel in my ways had walked!

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> “Soon their enemies I would have brought low, “And against their adversaries I would have turned my hand:

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> “The haters of Jehovah would have lied to him, “And their time should have been for ever:

<!-- PAGE 953 -->

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> “And I would have fed them with the fat of corn: “And from the rock with honey I would have satisfied thee.”

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 82</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Psalm of Asaph*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> God sitteth in the assembly of God: In the midst of the gods he will judge.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> How long will ye judge unjustly? And the faces of the ungodly will ye lift up? Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Judge the poor and the orphan; The helpless and the destitute justify ye.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Rescue the poor one and the afflicted one: From the hand of the ungodly ones deliver *them*.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> *But* they know not, neither do they understand *any thing*:  In darkness they walk, *Although* moved are all the foundations of the earth.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> As for me, I have said, “Ye are gods, “And children of the Most High all of you:

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> “Surely as a man ye shall die; “And as one [*of the people*,] O princes! ye shall fall.”

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">8</span> Arise, O God! judge the earth: For thou shalt inherit all nations.</p>

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 83</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Song [ορ Psalm, of Asaph*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> O God! keep not silence with thyself; Hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God!

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> For behold! thy enemies make a tumult: And those who hate thee have lifted up the head.

<!-- PAGE 954 -->

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Against thy people they have craftily formed a design, And have consulted against thy hidden ones.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> They have said, “Come and let us cut them off from being a nation; “And let there be no remembrance of the name of Israel any more.”

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> For they have consulted with the heart together; Against thee a covenant they have made.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> The tents of Edom, and of the Ishmaelites; Of Moab and of the Hagarenes.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek; The Philistines with the inhabitants of Tyre.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> Also Assur is associated with them: They have been an arm to the sons of Lot. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Do to them as to the Midianites, As to Sisera, as to Jabin, at the brook Kishon.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> They perished at Endor; They became manure for the earth.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Make them, [*even*] their princes, like Oreb, and like Zeeb; And like Zebah, and like Zalmunna, all their princes.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Who have said, “Let us take in possession for ourselves “The habitations of God.”

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> O my God! make them like a whirling ball; Like stubble before the wind.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> As fire burneth a forest, And as the flame kindleth the mountains, <span style="color:#800000">15</span> So pursue them with thy tempest, And with thy whirlwind terrify them.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> Fill their faces with shame; That they may seek thy name, O Jehovah!

<!-- PAGE 955 -->

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> Let them be ashamed, and terrified for ever;  <span style="color:#800000">ff105</span> And let them be confounded, and perish.

<span style="color:#800000">18</span> And let them know that thou, even thou, art, thy name Jehovah, Thou alone the Most High over all the earth.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 84</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To The Chief Musician Upon Gittith. A Psalm of the sons of Korah*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> How amiable are thy tabernacles, O Jehovah of armies!

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Long, yea, even faint doth my soul after the courts of Jehovah: My heart and my flesh leap for joy towards the living God.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Also the sparrow hath found a house for herself, And the swallow a nest for herself, Where she may place her young ones: O thine altars! thou Jehovah of armies! my King and my God!

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Blessed *are* those who dwell in thy house: Continually they will be praising thee. Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Blessed *is* the man whose strength is in thee; The ways [*are*] in their heart.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> They passing through the valley of weeping, will together make it a fountain; Also the cisterns the rain will cover.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> They will journey from strength to strength; Seen will be the God of gods in Zion.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> O Jehovah, God of armies! hear my prayer: Hearken, O God of Jacob! Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Our shield do thou behold, O God! And look upon the face of thy Christ.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> For better is one day in thy courts than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, Than dwell in the tents of ungodliness.

<!-- PAGE 956 -->

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> For a sun and shield *is* Jehovah God *to us*; Grace and glory give will Jehovah; He will not withhold *any* good from those who walk uprightly.

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> O Jehovah of armies! Blessed *is* the man who confideth in thee.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 85</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*To the Chief Musician. A Psalm of the sons of Korah*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Thou hast been favorable, O Jehovah! to thy land: Thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Thou hast taken away the iniquity of thy people: Thou hast covered all their sins. Selah <span style="color:#800000">3</span> Thou hast turned away all thy anger: Thou hast drawn back the fury of thy indignation.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">4</span> Turn us, O God of our salvation! And relax thy anger against us.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> Wilt thou for ever be angry with us? Wilt thou prolong thy wrath from age to age?

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Wilt not thou being turned *to us* quicken us? And thy people will rejoice in thee.

<span style="color:#800000">7</span> Show us, O Jehovah! thy mercy; and thy salvation grant unto us.

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> I will hear what God Jehovah will speak: Surely he will speak peace to his people and to his meek ones, And they will not return to folly.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> Surely near to those who fear him is his salvation, That dwell may glory in our land.

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> Mercy and truth shall meet together; Righteousness and peace shall kiss [*each other*.] <span style="color:#800000">11</span> Truth out of the earth shall spring up; And righteousness from heaven shall look down.

<!-- PAGE 957 -->

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> Likewise Jehovah will give that which is good: And our land shall yield her increase.

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> Righteousness before him shall go; And shall set in the way her steps.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 86</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Prayer of David*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> Incline, O Jehovah, thy ear, answer me; For poor and needy *am* I.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Keep my soul, for I am meek: O thou, my God! save thy servant who trusteth in thee.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Have compassion upon me, O Jehovah! For to thee do I cry daily.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> Gladden the soul of thy servant; For to thee, O Lord! my soul I lift up.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> For thou, O Lord! *art* good, and gracious, Plenteous in mercy to all who call upon thee.

<span style="color:#800000">6</span> Listen, O Jehovah! to my prayer, Attend to the voice of my supplications.

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">7</span> In the day of my trouble I will cry to thee: For thou wilt answer me.</p>

<span style="color:#800000">8</span> There is none like unto thee, O Lord! among the gods; And *there* is none [*who can work*] according to thy works.

<span style="color:#800000">9</span> All the nations which thou hast made shall come, And shall worship before thy face, O Lord! And glory they shall give to thy name:

<span style="color:#800000">10</span> For great art thou, And doing wonders, thou God alone.

<span style="color:#800000">11</span> Show me, O Jehovah! thy ways; I will walk in thy truth: Unite my heart to fear thy name.

<!-- PAGE 958 -->

<span style="color:#800000">12</span> I will celebrate thee, O Lord my God! with my whole heart; And I will glorify thy name for ever;

<span style="color:#800000">13</span> For thy mercy hath been great towards me; And thou hast delivered my soul from the lower grave.

<span style="color:#800000">14</span> O God! the proud have risen up against me, And a company of mighty men have sought after my soul; And they have not set thee before them.

<span style="color:#800000">15</span> And thou, O Lord! [*art*] a God compassionate and gracious; Slow to anger; and plenteous in mercy and truth.

<span style="color:#800000">16</span> Look to me, and have pity upon me: Give thy strength to thy servant, And save the son of thy handmaid.

<span style="color:#800000">17</span> Make with me a sign for good: And see shall my adversaries and be ashamed; For thou, O Jehovah! hast secured me and comforted me.

<p class="title-block-h2" style="text-align:center; font-size:16px; font-weight:bold; margin:18px 0 12px;" markdown="1"><span style="color:#006411">PSALM 87</span></p>

<p style="text-align:center; color:#000080; margin:14px 2em;"><span style="color:#000080">*A Psalm [ορ Song of the sons of Korah*</span></p>

<span style="color:#800000">1</span> His foundations [*are*] in the holy mountains.

<span style="color:#800000">2</span> Love doth Jehovah the gates of Zion More than all the tabernacles of Jacob.

<span style="color:#800000">3</span> Glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God! Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">4</span> I will make mention of Rahab, and Babel among those who know me: Behold the Philistines, and Tyre, with Ethiopia, He is born there! Selah.

<span style="color:#800000">5</span> And of Zion it shall be said, “Man and man is born in her; “And the Most High himself will establish her.”

<p style="text-align:center" markdown="1"><span style="color:#800000">6</span> The Lord will recount when he writeth the peoples, “He is born there.” Selah.</p>

<!-- PAGE 959 -->
